Goods, oil transporters’ strike threatens industry, exports
items.description: KARACHI: Goods carriers remain parked in Mauripur on Saturday, disrupting cargo movement to and from the city’s ports.—Online • Movement of over 400,000 goods-carrying vehicles suspended • Transporters refuse to end strike before talks with govt KARACHI: A countrywide strike by goods transporters and oil tankers started affecting industrial and export supply chains on Saturday, with operators vowing to continue the protest until the outcome of talks with the government on Monday, while manufacturers warned that prolonged disruption could halt production and jeopardise export commitments. Pakistan Goods Transporters Alliance Chairman Nisar Hussain Jafry told Dawn that “our countrywide strike will continue as our leadership intends to meet the ministers concerned with petroleum, transport and ports on Monday”. He said the movement of more than 400,000 goods-carrying vehicles, ranging from small to large, had been suspended from Saturday until the outcome of Monday’s meeting. “We have already unloaded our containers at the ports,” he said. Mr Jafry said goods transporters were striking over multiple issues, including the government’s recently introduced daily fuel price mechanism. “We are dissatisfied with the daily fuel price fixation introduced by the government, which is only creating problems,” he said. Since intercity movement of vehicles takes between one and three days, transporters and industries cannot make firm commitments on transportation charges because of daily changes in fuel prices, he said. Mr Jafry urged the government to restore the monthly fuel price mechanism and reduce withholding tax on transporters to 2pc from 7pc, noting that oil carriers were paying 2pc withholding tax on services. He said the government and goods transporters had signed a charter of demands in December 2025, but the commitments made under it had yet to be fulfilled. Mr Jafry also complained about the number of toll plazas, saying they had been established at intervals of around 30km and that transporters were perturbed over high toll rates. Transporters were also facing issues related to parking of heavy vehicles in areas surrounding the ports and driving licences, he added. Supply-chain disruption Already struggling with high production costs, industrialists warned that the nationwide strike by goods transporters could further disrupt industrial activity if supplies of raw materials remained suspended. They cautioned that prolonged disruption in cargo movement could paralyse factories, derail production schedules and jeopardise export commitments, ultimately affecting employment and the overall economy. SITE Association of Industry President Abdul Rehman Fudda said the strike had created an alarming situation for manufacturers. “The entire production system depends on timely supply of raw materials and delivery of finished goods. If factories fail to receive essential inputs, production will stall, while delays in dispatching finished products will worsen financial stress for industries,” he said. The export sector was already grappling with multiple challenges, Mr Fudda said, warning that if export consignments failed to reach buyers on time because of the transporters’ strike, industries could face penalties, price cuts or claims for damages. He urged the government to intervene urgently and resolve the dispute through negotiations with goods transporters. “Authorities must act before the situation escalates to the point where the country’s industry and supply chain collapse entirely. If the strike prolongs, the damage will extend beyond manufacturers — affecting exports, jobs and overall economic activity,” he said. Mr Fudda also called for immediate relief measures for the industrial sector, warning that rising production costs, expensive energy and policy uncertainty were putting the survival of industries at serious risk. He said escalating electricity and gas tariffs, rising production costs, high financing expenses and the absence of consistent economic policies had significantly undermined industrial activity. Despite these challenges, he said, the business community continued to keep the wheels of the economy moving, adding that further neglect of the industrial sector would be against the country’s economic interests. He called on the government to ensure energy supplies at competitive tariffs, simplify the tax regime, expedite payment of pending refunds, improve the ease of doing business and introduce investor-friendly policies. Published in Dawn, August 9th, 2026

items.title: Iran links Hormuz reopening to US meeting promises
items.description: • Pezeshkian insists now is ‘best time’ to end war as Iran ‘victorious’ • Tehran seeks US compensation, end to threats, lifting of sanctions • Muscat terms talks ‘positive’; Araghchi sees deal ‘very close’ • UAE accuses Iran of hitting another tanker • Trump’s top general seeks an ‘off-ramp’ from the war DUBAI: As Iran has linked the reopening of Strait of Hormuz to the Unites States meeting commitments, not to any deal with Oman on new shipping arrangements, President Masoud Pezeshkian said he believed this was the best time for an agreement. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran and Oman were “very close” to agreement on a new shipping route through the strait but that reopening it depended on other conditions, including US compensation to Iran. Tehran earlier on Saturday claimed an agreement with Oman on new shipping arrangements in the Strait of Hormuz was close but would not be enough to reopen the waterway. The claim comes at a time when the United Arab Emirates accused Iran of targeting a tanker belonging to its state-owned oil company in the strait, after an unknown projectile hit the vessel. Oman said negotiations with Iran about the future administration of the strait were “positive and constructive”, but warned against repeated attacks on shipping. Agreement between Iran and Oman over the strait is seen as vital to a wider deal to end the war that began with US and Israeli attacks on Iran on Feb 28 and led to Tehran establishing a chokehold over the major energy export route. A US official said on Friday Washington anticipated an agreement soon between Iran and Oman, which sit on either side of the strait, so that normal oil traffic could resume. The secretary of Iran’s top national security body, Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr, listed other demands including ending US threats against Iran, stopping aggression against Iran and its Lebanese, Palestinian, Yemeni and Iraqi allies, lifting a blockade and sanctions on Iran and freeing Iranian assets. Iran has imposed an effective blockade of the strait and wants to charge users for passage, repeatedly attacking ships it accuses of attempting to circumvent its preferred route. The US vehemently opposes any Iranian tolls in the strait, though a June deal struck by the warring parties does allow Tehran to hammer out arrangements for the “future administration” of Hormuz in dialogue with fellow coastal state Oman. Araghchi said the previous shipping traffic separation scheme through the strait was no longer acceptable to Tehran and that Iran was discussing a temporary route with Oman while technical and legal issues surrounding a permanent route were resolved. The Revolutionary Guards underscored the point, saying: “The opening of the Strait of Hormuz has its own mechanism and has nothing to do with the negotiations between Iran and Oman.” “The enemy is forced to accept Iran’s conditions for the opening of the strait and to refrain from the interference that it is currently making in the negotiations, which have almost reached their end, between Iran, Oman and other countries,” the Guards said. According to Iran’s Tasnim news agency, Guards spokesperson Hossein Mohebbi stressed that “whenever the United States accepts Iran’s conditions, the Strait of Hormuz will certainly be reopened”. “There is cohesion, stren­gth and unity in the country, and as far as I know, Iran is considered victorious and powerful in this war,” Mr Pezeshkian said. US officials debate risks US Vice President J.D. Vance said a potential understanding with Iran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz to normal commercial traffic, while former defence secretary Mark Esper warned against giving Iran and Oman a role in administering the strategic waterway. Vance told Fox News ’ “Saturday in America” that Washington expected oil and gas shipments through the strait to return to pre-war levels, saying Iran had assured the US that it had no plans to impose tolls on shipping. “Our expectation is you’re going to see the same amount of oil and gas come out of the Gulf that you saw before the conflict started,” Vance said. “That is what the Iranians have told us that they are going to do.” He cautioned, however, that Washington would judge Tehran by its actions rather than its assurances. Meanwhile, Esper, appearing Friday on Fox News ’ “America Reports”, warned against any arrangement that would give Iran and Oman control over traffic through the strait. He said reports indicated that Tehran and Muscat were nearing an agreement that could divide passage through the waterway, with a northern route leading into the Persian Gulf and a southern route running along Oman’s coast. “They may or may not charge a fee, but they would administer and control it in one way, shape or form, which would be a very bad outcome for us,” Esper said. Amid the optimism and warning, CNN reported that Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Gen Dan Caine has privately been seeking an “off-ramp” from the war, warning Trump administration officials that available military options may not be sufficient to achieve the president’s stated objectives. Citing three sources familiar with the matter, CNN reported that Caine had discussed finding an “off-ramp” with Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Vance and CIA Director John Ratcliffe. With input from Anwar Iqbal Published in Dawn, August 9th, 2026

items.title: NADMO sounds flood alert ahead of Bagre Dam spillage
items.description: The National Disaster Management Organisation (NADMO) has begun preparations to mitigate possible flooding in the North East Region following notification from Burkina Faso that the Bagre Dam will be opened from Tuesday, August 11, 2026. The planned spillage is expected to increase the volume of water entering Ghana through the White Volta River and its tributaries, potentially raising water levels in communities situated along waterways and other flood-prone locations. In an alert issued by its North East Regional Office, NADMO urged residents, farmers, fishermen, herdsmen and other persons operating in vulnerable areas to take immediate precautionary measures to safeguard lives and property. “The National Disaster Management Organisation (NADMO), North East Regional Office, wishes to inform the general public that the authorities responsible for the Bagre Dam in Burkina Faso have officially notified Ghana that the Bagre Dam will be spilt from Tuesday, 11th August, 2026. “NADMO therefore strongly advises all residents, farmers, fishermen, herdsmen, and other persons living or working along riverbanks and low-lying areas to take precautionary measures,” the statement said. Move to safer areas NADMO said the increased downstream flow could result in rising water levels and flooding, particularly in communities along the White Volta and its tributaries. “The spillage is expected to increase the volume of water flowing downstream into Ghana through the White Volta River and its tributaries. Communities located along riverbanks and flood-prone areas may experience rising water levels, which could result in flooding,” it added. The organisation consequently advised people living in vulnerable locations to relocate to safer areas before the situation worsened. Residents were also cautioned against entering river channels and floodplains for farming, fishing, animal grazing or other activities. “Do not farm, fish, graze animals, or undertake any activity within river channels and floodplains,” NADMO cautioned. Farmers whose farms are located along riverbanks have, in particular, been encouraged to take steps to harvest their crops early where necessary to minimise losses. “Farmers farming along the river banks are advised to harvest their farm produce earlier when necessary before the dam is spilt,” NADMO said. The organisation further urged residents to move valuables, foodstuffs, livestock and farm equipment away from areas considered vulnerable to flooding. It also warned the public not to attempt crossing flooded roads, rivers, streams or bridges, while calling for strict compliance with safety directives issued by NADMO, the security agencies, district assemblies and other relevant authorities. Public education intensified NADMO said district offices across the North East Region had been directed to intensify public education and sensitisation, particularly in communities located along the White Volta and other vulnerable waterways. The organisation said it would continue to monitor the situation and provide updates to the public as developments unfold.

items.title: Banques : le déficit de liquidité s'allège à 134,3 MMDH du 29 juillet au 5 août
items.description: Le déficit de liquidité bancaire moyen a poursuivi son allègement, reculant de 2,7% à 134,3 milliards de dirhams (MMDH) durant la période du 29 juillet au 5 août, selon BMCE Capital Global Research (BKGR). Cette évolution intervient au moment où les avances à 7 jours de Bank Al-Maghrib (BAM) affichent une hausse de 9,8 MMDH pour s'établir à 53,9 MMDH, indique BKGR dans sa récente note « Fixed Income Weekly ». De leur côté, les placements du Trésor ont diminué avec un encours quotidien maximal de 9,6 MMDH, contre 16,5 MMDH la semaine précédente, précise la même source. Le taux moyen pondéré (TMP) est resté stable à 2,25%, tandis que le MONIA (Moroccan Overnight Index Average : indice monétaire de référence au jour le jour, calculé sur la base des transactions de pensions livrées ayant comme collatéral les bons du Trésor) a reculé pour atteindre 2,156%. Au cours de la prochaine période, BAM devrait diminuer le rythme de ses interventions sur le marché monétaire, fixant le volume de ses avances à 7 jours à 49,4 MMDH, contre 53,9 MMDH précédemment. The post Banques : le déficit de liquidité s'allège à 134,3 MMDH du 29 juillet au 5 août appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.description: Musician Choirmaster has paid a deeply emotional tribute to his late wife, actress and entrepreneur Beverly Ama Afaglo-Baah, remembering her as a loving, generous and deeply faithful woman whose strength and compassion transformed his life. Delivering his final tribute at the funeral service for Beverly at the forecourt of the State House in Accra on Saturday, August 8, Choirmaster reflected on the life they shared and the family they built together. He expressed gratitude for the support, encouragement and prayers his wife offered him throughout their marriage, saying her influence had strengthened his faith and shaped him in profound ways. “Thank you for your encouragement of the beautiful family we built together. Thank you for every prayer, every act of kindness; you strengthened my faith,” he said. While Beverly was widely recognised for her achievements in the entertainment industry, Choirmaster said he knew and cherished the woman behind the public persona, someone whose generosity was not driven by a desire for recognition. “Many knew you as a gifted actress and an endearing actress. But I knew of the beautiful heart behind every achievement. You loved deeply and gave generously. And you never once sought recognition,” he said. He also paid tribute to her contribution to Ghana’s film industry, noting the impact of her work on audiences and highlighting her involvement in Traffic Shawarma . “Through your acting and film works, you touched countless hearts with hope and kindness, especially with Traffic Shawarma,” he said. ‘You never stopped trusting God’ Choirmaster’s tribute also centred on Beverly’s faith and resilience during her battle with illness. He recalled how, despite the difficulties she faced, she continued to hold on to her faith and became a source of strength for him during moments of fear and uncertainty. “Even in the midst of your battle, you never stopped trusting God. You comforted me when I was afraid. Your resilience, courage, and steadfast belief in God’s promises inspire me every day,” he said. He said witnessing his wife’s courage through her illness had left an indelible mark on him. “Witnessing your strength has changed me forever. Rest well, my queen. I love you,” he added. The funeral brought together personalities from Ghana’s entertainment, business and political circles, who joined family and friends to mourn the actress and entrepreneur. Among those who attended were Yvonne Nelson, Van Vicker, music duo Keche, Rex Omar, Obour, Eunice Banini, Jackie Appiah, Captain Planet of 4×4, businessman Ibrahim Mahama, Selassie Ibrahim, Nana Ama McBrown, Adjetey Annan, Roselyn Ngissah and John Dumelo, the Member of Parliament for Ayawaso West Wuogon, among others. Beverly Ama Afaglo-Baah died on Sunday, May 24, 2026, aged 42. Her death triggered an outpouring of grief across Ghana’s entertainment industry, with colleagues, friends and fans remembering her for her work as an actress and entrepreneur and her contribution to the creative industry.

items.title: Le Maroc consolide sa place parmi les principaux fournisseurs d'engrais de la Turquie
items.description: Le Maroc figure parmi les principaux fournisseurs d'engrais de la Turquie, se classant au deuxième rang au mois de juin 2026, selon l'agence russe RIA Novosti, basée sur les statistiques officielles turques. D'après ces données, les exportations marocaines d'engrais vers la Turquie ont atteint 24,4 millions de dollars, le plaçant comme le deuxième principal fournisseurs du marché turc. Le Royaume devance ainsi plusieurs exportateurs majeurs, dont le Turkménistan (8,04 millions de dollars) et Oman (6,4 millions de dollars). Seule la Chine a enregistré des ventes supérieures sur le marché turc durant cette période, avec 25,5 millions de dollars. La Russie occupe, quant à elle, la troisième position avec des exportations d'engrais évaluées à 19,9 millions de dollars en juin. Selon RIA Novosti, les livraisons russes vers la Turquie ont été multipliées par plus de quatre par rapport au même mois de 2025 et ont progressé de 70 % par rapport au mois de mai 2026. Au cours du premier semestre 2026, les exportations russes d'engrais vers la Turquie ont totalisé 182,3 millions de dollars, soit un léger recul de 3 % en glissement annuel, précise encore l'agence. Ces chiffres confirment la place du Maroc parmi les principaux acteurs du commerce international des engrais, un secteur dans lequel le Royaume occupe une position stratégique grâce à ses importantes réserves de phosphate et à son industrie de transformation, lui permettant de répondre à une demande croissante sur plusieurs marchés internationaux. items.title: Prince Kofi Amoabeng Leadership Foundation opens applications for Cohort 4
items.description: The PK Amoabeng Leadership Foundation has opened applications for the fourth cohort of its flagship Scholars Programme, a one-year leadership initiative aimed at developing ethical, disciplined and resilient young leaders for Ghana and Africa. The foundation, established by Captain (Rtd.) Prince Kofi Amoabeng, said the programme was designed to respond to what he considers a critical leadership deficit that threatens Africa’s development potential. In a release on August 4, 2026, Executive Director of the PK Amoabeng Leadership Foundation, Rachael Awinsu Alabilla, said the programme targets high-potential individuals between 18 and 40 years, with selected scholars undergoing an intensive curriculum intended to equip them with the integrity, resilience and leadership skills needed to contribute meaningfully to society. Unlike programmes focused solely on classroom instruction, the Scholars Programme combines military training, leadership boot camps, one-on-one mentorship, job shadowing, cultural immersion and leadership seminars. The foundation said its broader objective is to nurture ethical, entrepreneurial and patriotic leaders capable of influencing positive change and helping to transform the future of the continent. It said its core values — Integrity, Professionalism, Innovation and Respect for All — are integrated into every aspect of the year-long programme. Application details Applications for Cohort 4 opened on August 3, 2026, and will close on September 15, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. GMT. Applicants must be between 18 and 40 years and are required to pay a non-refundable application fee of GH¢100. Applications can be submitted through the foundation’s designated application portal. items.title: Whose time is it? By Patrick Omorodion
items.description: There is a saying in our local parlance that ‘if one man own no spoil, another man own no go better’.? This means that “One man’s loss is another man’s gain.” In 2015, then president of FIFA, Joseph Sepp Blatter was in his fifth term as president of football’s world body when he ran into hot waters of financial scandals. He was investigated for a controversial 2-million Swiss franc payment made to then UEFA president Michel Platini. Both of them were tried and however, cleared of fraud charges by a Swiss federal court. The probe was part of broader racketeering, wire fraud, and money laundering investigations into FIFA officials, which led to Blatter’s resignation in 2015 after he was suspended. Then senior vice president and CAF president, Issa Hayatou took over in acting capacity pending the election in 2016. Hayatou did not step forward to contest mainly because of his failing health.. One expected that since the most senior vice president, Hayatou, who was then CAF president was not contesting, African federations would support the only African who joined the race, Mosima Gabriel “Tokyo” Sexwale, a South African businessman. No. Instead CAF threw their weight behind Gianni Infantino, a Swiss like Blatter. As a result, Sexwale withdrew from the race even before voting started. Europe naturally backed Infantino who was their own. But because of the backing of Africa for oil rich Bahrain candidate and president of the Asian Confederation, Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim Al Khalifa, Infantino couldn’t win at the first ballot. At the time, FIFA congress had 207 total votes and Infantino won in the second round with a majority vote of 115, ostensibly from the African voters who switched after the first ballot sensing that their first choice wasn’t going to clinch it. Ten years after, again about a year to the FIFA election, its president is embroiled in another controversy which is looking likely to consume him especially as his home con- federation, UEFA is leading the assault. Their initial grouse was that Infantino was allowing US president Donald Trump interfere with the organization of their cherished product, the World Cup. They kicked when Infantino allowed a referee’s decision on the pitch to be upturned after a telephone call by Trump. With all that happened during the World Cup and earned him enemies, Infantino didn’t allow the anger to douse but quickly contrived a plan to sell a 21% stake in future World Cup revenues to private investors without consulting other stakeholders. This was the last straw that has led to a plethora of calls for his resignation. So when the 211 (up from 207 in 2016) member associations gather in Rabat, Morocco in March next year for the FIFA Congress to elect the next FIFA president, will Infantino survive as those who had earlier pledged their support are withdrawing it now? FIFA’s current Vice Presidents are Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa (Senior Vice-President, from AFC- Asia), Alejandro Domínguez ( CONMEBOL – South America), Aleksander Čeferin ( UEFA- Europe(, Lambert Maltock (OFC- Oceania) Patrice Motsepe (CAF -Africa), Victor Montagliani ( CONCACAF – Central/ North America and the Caribbeans) as well as Sándor Csányi and Debbie Hewitt, both also from UEFA. Sheikh Salman contested against Infantino in 2016 but lost. Is he ready to challenge him again this time as his Europe base is at ‘war’ with him and have lost confidence in him? Already Europe as well as Central/North America have vouched to withdraw their support for him, with Europe threatening to withdraw from the World Cup if he remains FIFA president. Though South America have voiced their disapproval of his style of communication, they said they won’t withdraw their support for him. Africa are united in their support for his commercialization plan which they say would help them get funds for football development, as well as his ambition for another term in office. As it is now, who will last laugh, UEFA or Infantino? UEFA is the most powerful bloc in FIFA because the bulk of money for the body’s activities comes from Europe. If CONCACAF joins them, there is not much CAF and CONMEBOL would do to swing victory for Infantino. The 211 confederations’ votes are divided among the six regional groups thus: Europe – 55 votes, Africa – 54 votes, Asia – 47 votes, North/Central America and the Caribbeans – 35 votes, South America – 10 votes and Oceania – 10 votes. With Europe, Asia and North & Central America with the Caribbean countries already at daggers drawn with Infan- tino, votes of Africa, South America and Oceania delegates won’t save Infantino from defeat, all things being equal. But who are the likely opposition candidates Europe, the champions of ‘Infantino must go’, as it were, is looking at? Even though no candidate has declared his or her interest in the race, the names that have popped up include Nasser Al-Khelaïfi, Paris Saint-Germain president, Aleksander Čeferin, UEFA president and a leading critic of Infantino. The only woman in the picture is Lise Klaveness, the out- spoken president of the Norwegian Football Association who also announced the withdrawal of her support for Infantino. From CONCACAF, is their president and FIFA vice president Victor Montagliani, a Canadian businessman. Skeikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al-Khalifa apart from being president of the Asian Football Confederation, is the Senior vice president of FIFA. He was up against Infantino before but will he try his luck again next year, especially as he has been in the forefront of those pushing back against some of Infantino’s controversial ideas. So the question is, whose time is it? The post Whose time is it? By Patrick Omorodion appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Jorge Vilda se félicite de la qualification pour le Mondial 2027
items.description: Le sélectionneur de l'équipe nationale féminine, Jorge Vilda, s'est félicité de la qualification, samedi, des Lionnes de l'Atlas au Mondial 2027, affirmant que c'est le fruit du projet de développement du football féminin mené par la Fédération Royale Marocaine de Football (FRMF). S'exprimant lors de la conférence de presse d'après-match des quarts de finale remporté 2-1 face à l’Afrique du Sud, Vilda a expliqué que l'accès au Mondial était le premier objectif de la sélection nationale, tout en saluant le soutien massif du public tout au long de la rencontre. Concernant le déroulement du match, le sélectionneur national a souligné que l'équipe du Maroc a réalisé une très bonne première mi-temps, marquée par une meilleure maîtrise du jeu et la création de plusieurs occasions, tout en félicitant la ligne défensive pour sa capacité à neutraliser le danger de l'attaque sud-africaine durant la majeure partie du match. Le scénario du match a changé après le deuxième but, lorsque la sélection sud-africaine s'est projetée en force vers l'attaque et a engagé un plus grand nombre de joueuses sur la ligne offensive, ce qui a contraint les éléments nationaux à reculer et à se replier en défense, a-t-il ajouté. S'agissant de la demi-finale, Vilda a précisé que le Maroc connaîtrait son adversaire à l'issue de l'affiche Nigéria-Cameroun, affirmant que l'équipe nationale connaît bien ces deux sélections pour les avoir déjà affrontées, et que la priorité actuelle sera la récupération physique et mentale des joueuses. Pour rappel, la sélection nationale affrontera en demi-finale le vainqueur du match Cameroun-Nigéria, mercredi au Stade Moulay El Hassan à Rabat, à partir de 21h00. items.title: Can NDC Resolve Growing Concerns in Abia State Before 2027?
items.description: By Phillip Ogbonna As Nigeria gradually moves toward the 2027 general elections, political parties are expected to strengthen their internal structures, inspire confidence among their members, and present themselves as credible alternatives to the electorate. In Abia State, however, concerns are beginning to emerge within the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), prompting important discussions about fairness, inclusiveness, internal democracy, and the party’s electoral strategy. Across various parts of the state, conversations among party members have increasingly focused on whether recent decisions concerning the allocation of party tickets reflect the principles of equity, justice, and balanced representation that many believe should guide a growing political movement. While every political party has the right to nominate candidates it considers best positioned to win elections, many stakeholders maintain that the selection process should also foster unity and ensure that all communities feel fairly represented. One issue receiving considerable attention is the situation in the Abia North Senatorial District, particularly within the Arochukwu axis. According to concerns raised by some party members, both the House of Representatives ticket and the Abia State House of Assembly ticket were reportedly allocated to aspirants from Atani community in Arochukwu. Critics argue that this decision overlooked the aspirant who reportedly emerged victorious in the NDC primary election for the Arochukwu State Constituency and is from Ututu, a clan that, according to supporters, has never produced a member of the Abia State House of Assembly and is widely believed to be due for the opportunity under the principle of political rotation. Although party leaders may have had reasons for their decisions, critics contend that such an arrangement could create perceptions of exclusion among other communities that have equally invested their time, resources, and commitment in building the party. For many political observers, candidate selection goes beyond choosing individuals for elective office. It is also about managing diversity, promoting inclusiveness, and strengthening public confidence in the party’s internal democratic processes. When committed members begin to question whether fairness and equity have been adequately considered, party leaders have a responsibility to engage with those concerns openly and transparently. Several stakeholders argue that concentrating key elective positions within a single community may unintentionally weaken the sense of belonging among supporters from other villages and wards. They warn that members who feel marginalized may become less motivated during campaigns, potentially reducing the grassroots support that often determines the outcome of closely contested elections. Political success is rarely achieved through individual popularity alone; it is built on collective effort, shared ownership, and the confidence that every stakeholder has a meaningful place within the party. These concerns are reportedly not limited to Arochukwu alone. Similar questions surrounding zoning, political balance, and candidate selection have allegedly emerged in other parts of Abia State. Many party members believe that addressing these issues proactively would strengthen, rather than weaken, the NDC. They point to dialogue, transparency, and genuine reconciliation as proven approaches that have enabled political parties to overcome internal disagreements ahead of major elections. Those advocating for a review insist that their position should not be interpreted as opposition to the party. Rather, they describe their concerns as a constructive appeal for reforms that would make the NDC more united, inclusive, and electorally competitive. They argue that overlooking widely accepted and popular aspirants could diminish the party’s appeal in communities where local acceptance and grassroots support are essential to electoral success. The questions being raised by many members are straightforward yet significant. Is the NDC making decisions that maximize its chances of electoral success across Abia State? Has sufficient consideration been given to equity, inclusiveness, political acceptability, and long-term electoral strategy? Most importantly, can the party reassure its members that every aspirant received fair and equal consideration throughout the nomination process? These are legitimate questions that deserve thoughtful and transparent responses. Successful political parties understand that unity cannot simply be demanded; it must be built through fairness, accountability, transparency, and mutual respect. Members who dedicate their time, resources, and commitment to building a political platform naturally expect decisions that reflect the collective interest rather than the interests of a select few. As preparations for the 2027 elections gather momentum, many loyal party faithful believe this is the appropriate time for both the national and state leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress to engage members openly, clarify the rationale behind key decisions, and reassure stakeholders that the party remains committed to justice, equity, inclusiveness, and internal democracy. Such engagement could help restore confidence, ease tensions, and reinforce the unity required to effectively compete in the forthcoming elections. Ultimately, elections are won not only through campaign promises but also through the level of confidence, cohesion, and trust that exists within a political party. How the Nigeria Democratic Congress responds to these growing concerns in Abia State may ultimately determine whether it enters the 2027 general elections as a united political force capable of inspiring voters or as a party still grappling with avoidable internal divisions. items.title: Interior Minister’s achievements have projected youths positively
items.description: By Saka Ola Ahmed The Minister of Interior, Dr Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, achievements in his ministry in the last three years have created a positive image for youths in the country and have shown that, when given responsibility , they can excel. The unprecedented positive performance so far in the Ministry of Interior by the Minister has given everyone hope that the youths can successfully lead and rule the country. It is the belief of many, therefore , that the Minister is currently the most suitable person to facilitate the development of Ondo State, where he is from. Hon. Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, Minister of Interior, is a Nigerian engineer, entrepreneur, philanthropist, and politician . He was a member of the House of Representatives representing Akoko North East/Akoko North West Federal Constituency of Ondo State from 2019 to 2023. Dr Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo was appointed minister by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in August 2023. His ministry oversees the Nigeria Immigration Service, Nigerian Correctional Service, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), and Federal Fire Service. The Minister has been honoured by different organisations for introducing important reforms, which are very beneficial. These include the digitization of the passport application process, deployment of airport e-Gates, and initiatives to clear extensive passport backlogs. In correctional service, he has pioneered major decongestion efforts at correctional centres by spearheading. programmes that paid fines to release thousands of inmates held for petty offences, alongside modernizing facilities. On Border and Asset Security, Hon Tunji-Ojo has focused on integrating intelligence data, enhancing border security, and using the NSCDC to protect critical national infrastructure. During his first term in the House of Representatives, he was the chairman of the House Committee on Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC). On 26 February 2023, he was re-elected as the federal lawmaker representing Akoko North East and North West Federal Constituency. However, he resigned his membership of the lower chamber of the National Assembly after being appointed by President Bola Tinubu as minister of Interior on 16 August 2023. Before going into politics, Tunji-Ojo was a business and management executive with a career in ICT, becoming the CEO of a leading indigenous ICT consultant company in Nigeria, Matrix IT Solutions Limited, at the age of 24. As a professional, he holds a certification in Ethical Hacking and Counter Measures. He is also a certified CompTIA Network Plus Engineer and a Britannia Hardware A+ Management Certificate Holder. His introduction of contactless passport renewal system for Nigerians living in Europe has endeared him to Nigerians in the diaspora. The system allows eligible Nigerians in Europe to renew their passports online without visiting any physical office, following the successful rollout of the initiative in Canada. The Minister has helped in fighting insecurity in the country. To further strengthen border surveillance, 30 new patrol vehicles have been commissioned, while a new Command and Control Centre, housing a 1.4 petabyte-capacity data center, has been constructed at the Nigerian Immigration Service, NIS, headquarters in Abuja. The Ministry has also activated the role of Document Verification Officers (DVOs) to authenticate passport applicants from their local government areas. Technological advancement has been a key focus of the Minister, culminating in the commissioning of the President Bola Ahmed Tinubu Technology Innovation Complex (BATTIC) on the 11th of December,2024. The facility houses the NIS Command and Control Center, ECOWAS Biometric Card Production Centre, the Interior Data Centre, the Visa Application Centre, and a solar farm. For his efforts and achievements, Dr Tunji-Ojo was named amongst the 30 most influential young Nigerians by the National Youth Council of Nigeria in 2019. He was also awarded as Pacesetter in Political Representation by Akoko North West Local Government Council, Okeagbe Akoko, Ondo State , in 2019. He got the Sir Ahmadu Bello Platinum Leadership Award of Excellence in 2019, National Assembly Best Legislator of the year in 2020, 2021, and the Kwame Nkrumah Leadership Award as “Worthy Ambassador of African 2010 Youth” by All African Students Union ,(AASU). items.title: Chinda most suitable for Rivers Brick House
items.description: By Caleb Ekesunnie Rt. Hon. Kingsley Ogundu Chinda current member of the House of Representatives, representing Obio/ Akpor Federal Constituency, Rivers State has been in the news lately for good reasons. He emerged a few months ago as the Rivers State gubernatorial candidate of All Progressives Congress (APC) for the 2027 general elections . He is the immediate past Minority Leader of the current 10th House of Representatives. He has used his over a decade and half stints in the National Assembly to demonstrate his preparedness to occupy the Rivers Brick House in a remarkable manner. As minority leader of the House, he showed his leadership dexterities to the admiration of his colleagues by introducing a brand of opposition leadership style that was largely innovative, moderate and strategic. Accordingly, Chinda provided an alternative legislative governance model that is inherently harmonious as a result boosted the bargaining power of members of the opposition in the House. This creative leadership paradigm distinguished him so exceedingly in the House. He remains one of the most outspoken members of the House. Chinda always finds his voice on the floor of the House and is one of the notable lawmakers who have contributed immensely in reshaping National Assembly as an institution in a considerable manner. Besides his exceptional leadership style, since 2011 he has been in the House Chinda has demonstrated unmatched legislative results. These productive legislative years at the National Assembly obviously accounted for his chain of re-elections into the legislative house His legislative governance abilities and prowess in the areas of parliamentary debates, processes, oversight functions , motions and Bills pursuits are uncommon. This legislative record underlines Chinda as one of the foremost Nigerian parliamentarians Over the years in NASS, Chinda has chaired the Public Accounts Committee of the House of Representatives and served as leader of the opposition before he decamped to the ruling APC. The vast experience he has obtained from legislative stewardship would be the gain of his Rivers people when elected and accordingly sworn in as Governor balanced, visionary and forthright, Chinda is known for his collegial, consensual and positive approach to governance. As a team player he would enlist the buy-in of a wide spectrum of Rivers people to fast-pace the state development when elected. As a leading parliamentarian, Chinda has imbibed legislative principles of collectivity, consensus and compromise. He would obviously bring these democratic virtues to fore when he takes charge at the Brick House when elected and sworn in, Chinda would prove to Rivers people that a robust background in the legislature is indispensable to drive state development. Chinda would certainly break barriers, dismantle bureaucracy and its hurdles and delays to put infrastructures in place in the state Chinda would not spend his first hundred days wrestling with structural gridlock, fighting with the members of the state legislature. He has enough experience to tame the initial challenges As a legislator, Chinda has for years watched endless brilliant ideas die in legislative committees, unutilized due to institutional wrangling to the detriment of the people; when he becomes Governor such ideas would be brought to fore for utilization for the benefit of Rivers people having groomed on executive/legislative relationship management over time. In bringing this time-honed legislative experience to bear on state responsibilities and imperatives, he would not just build roads and fund social services, he would ochestrate and build statutory architecture that endures and outlives his administration. This would be achieved through the introduction of state laws that would be best focused on needs assessment and reform development strategy . When elected, Chinda would treat every major development initiative and goal as permanent piece of policy tightly engineered to anchor and sustain executive strategy in the overall interest of Rivers people. Honourable Chinda is not new to the dynamics and workings of the executive arm of government; he had been a Commissioner for Environment where he effectively used state-level authority to regulate what was within the legal jurisdiction of the federal government by implementing actionable state environmental laws as it partains to waste generation and management of local and industrial pollution by forcing the bounds of federal actors with regards to continuous gas flaring and emissions, enforcement of strict compliance with environmental impact assessments (EIAs) for state-level infrastructure works through litigation, formal petitions, regulations and above all sustained citizen enlightenment and sensitisation. He would therefore be symbolic of converging executive and legislative action, a melting-pot of a formidable experience of both the executive and legislative arms of government. It is worthy to note that he is an astute lawyer, a human and civil rights advocate with a bias in public interest advocacy committed to fighting systemic injustice and underseved communities, giving voice to the voiceless, indigents and individuals living in poverty, marginalised or minority communities, non- profit organizations and charities as well as environmental rights’ groups and a host of others. With his vast experience in governance, legislative responsibilities and civil society sector, Rt Hon Kingsley Chinda is indeed most fitting to serve and save Rivers State today. He represents Rivers brand and pearl. The votes of Rivers people for him would strengthen his resolve to bring unprecedented and positive change to the oil rich state. items.title: Casablanca lance un mégaprojet de 1,5 milliard de dollars pour transformer ses déchets en électricité
items.description: La capitale économique va se doter d'une centrale de valorisation énergétique des déchets, portée par un consortium réunissant des partenaires helvético-japonais, marocains et japonais. Prévue pour entrer en service à la mi-2030, cette infrastructure ambitionne de réduire l'impact environnemental de la décharge de Mediouna tout en produisant de l'électricité pour près d'un million de personnes. La ville de Casablanca franchit une nouvelle étape dans sa transition énergétique et environnementale. Un consortium conduit par le groupe helvético-japonais Kanadevia Inova, aux côtés de l'énergéticien marocain Nareva et de la maison de négoce japonaise Itochu, a signé une convention de concession avec la commune de Casablanca pour la réalisation d'une usine de valorisation énergétique des déchets représentant un investissement de 1,5 milliard de dollars. Selon Reuters, les travaux devraient débuter avant la fin de l'année, sous réserve de la finalisation du montage financier. La mise en exploitation complète de l'installation est attendue à la mi-2030. Une infrastructure parmi les plus importantes d'Afrique Présentée comme la deuxième installation de ce type sur le continent africain, la future centrale traitera environ 1,5 million de tonnes de déchets ménagers par an. Elle produira près de 115 mégawatts d'électricité grâce à une combinaison de déchets, de biogaz issu de la décharge et d'énergie solaire, soit une capacité suffisante pour alimenter près d'un million d'habitants. Au-delà de la production électrique, le projet vise à réduire les impacts environnementaux de la décharge de Mediouna, la plus importante du Royaume. Situé en périphérie de Casablanca, ce site est depuis plusieurs décennies à l'origine de nuisances olfactives et de pollutions affectant les terrains agricoles voisins. La décomposition des déchets y génère également d'importantes émissions de méthane, un gaz à effet de serre au fort pouvoir réchauffant. Un financement principalement marocain Le lancement du chantier reste conditionné à la sécurisation des financements en fonds propres et en dette, attendue au cours du quatrième trimestre 2026. Dans un entretien accordé à Reuters, le directeur général de Kanadevia Inova, Bruno-Frédéric Baudouin, a indiqué que la dette serait entièrement levée auprès d'établissements bancaires marocains. Le consortium a également conclu un contrat d'achat de l'électricité produite avec l'Office national de l'électricité et de l'eau potable (ONEE). Les travaux de construction seront confiés au groupe marocain Somagec et devraient s'étendre sur environ trois ans et demi. Les premières opérations de traitement des déchets et de production d'électricité pourraient toutefois démarrer entre six et dix mois avant la livraison définitive du site. Un bénéfice climatique mis en avant Les promoteurs du projet estiment que la future installation permettra de réduire sensiblement les émissions de gaz à effet de serre liées à la décharge de Mediouna. Selon Bruno-Frédéric Baudouin, les réductions d'émissions pourraient représenter un volume équivalent à près de 20 % des émissions annuelles de la Suisse, soit, selon son image, « l'équivalent du retrait de 300.000 voitures de la circulation » . Cette estimation n'a toutefois pas fait l'objet d'une évaluation indépendante rendue publique. La valorisation énergétique des déchets continue néanmoins d'alimenter le débat parmi les spécialistes de l'environnement. Plusieurs chercheurs, organisations climatiques et collectifs de riverains estiment que ce type d'infrastructure, reposant majoritairement sur l'incinération, peut ralentir le développement du recyclage tout en générant des émissions de particules fines et de gaz à effet de serre. The post Casablanca lance un mégaprojet de 1,5 milliard de dollars pour transformer ses déchets en électricité appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: GLO@23: The Bull still reigns supreme
items.description: By Bodex Hungbo In a corporate world where corporate giants regularly swap boardrooms like trading cards and sell off equity at the first sign of volatility, one legendary tycoon continues to prove that absolute control is the ultimate power move. That man is Otunba Mike Adenuga Jr., the visionary billionaire whose dense belief in indigenous enterprise gave birth to Globacom, the telecom powerhouse affectionately known across the continent as Glo. As Globacom marks a monumental 23-year milestone, the spotlight shines brightly not only on the company’s extraordinary ascent, but on the enduring legacy of its founder. Adenuga stands as the only Nigerian to establish, nurture, and retain 100% sole ownership of a national telecommunications network; one that has evolved into one of Africa’s most recognizable, resilient, and influential brands. While rival networks scrambled through endless corporate restructuring, foreign buyouts, hostile takeovers, and high-stakes rebrandings, “The Bull” pulled off what many in international finance considered impossible; holding complete control of Nigeria’s proudest homegrown tech giant for over two decades without surrendering a single inch of authority. From the very beginning, Adenuga refused to follow the standard playbook written by foreign multinationals. When Globacom officially launched in August 2003, the market was heavily dominated by well-funded international operators who insisted that certain consumer-friendly models were economically impossible in Africa. Skeptics openly declared that a wholly indigenous, single-owner startup could never go toe-to-toe with established global giants. Adenuga didn’t just compete; he single-handedly revolutionized the entire landscape. At a time when competitors claimed that charging consumers per second rather than per minute was technically unfeasible, Glo introduced per-second billing on day one. By charging 1 kobo per second, Globacom shattered the status quo overnight, forcing the entire telecom industry to follow suit. That single disruptive move democratized mobile access, saved everyday Nigerians billions of Naira, and transformed mobile phones from luxury items for the elite into essential tools for the masses. Adenuga’s commitment to self-reliance went far beyond marketing strategies; it was backed by monumental capital investments in hard infrastructure. To ensure that Glo would never be beholden to external actors, he funded game-changing projects directly from his own vision and capital. Chief among these milestones was the construction of Glo-1, a multi-million-dollar, high-capacity submarine fiber-optic cable stretching over 9,800 kilometers directly from the United Kingdom to Nigeria. Single-handedly funded without taking a single dollar in foreign equity, Glo-1 provided West Africa with unprecedented broadband capacity, drastically improving internet speeds, powering corporate enterprises, and anchoring the region’s digital economy. Alongside this undersea marvel, Globacom built an extensive terrestrial fiber-optic backbone across Nigeria, expanding coverage into underserved rural communities and providing the critical pipeline for modern data services, mobile banking, and digital commerce. The fierce independence that defines Globacom is a direct reflection of its founder’s personal journey. Adenuga’s rise is the ultimate story of relentless African grit. Long before he was dubbed “The Bull” of African commerce, a young Adenuga drove taxis and worked security jobs in the United States to pay his way through university. Returning to Nigeria with a sharp mind and an insatiable work ethic, he built his fortune brick by brick. He conquered hard commodities, established a presence in oil and gas with Conoil, mastered corporate banking, and ultimately turned his sight toward telecommunications. Every venture was driven by the same philosophy: absolute dedication, hands-on execution, and a fierce refusal to settle for second best. Despite commanding a multi-billion-dollar fortune, Adenuga remains famously reclusive. Operating largely away from public cameras and party circuits, he chooses to let his work speak for him. His quiet philanthropy, strategic investments, and relentless job creation have lifted thousands of families and injected vital energy into the broader West African economy. Beyond cell towers and fiber-optic lines, Globacom transformed itself into an iconic symbol of African pride. Recognizing the power of local culture long before global streaming platforms arrived, Adenuga turned Glo into the largest single corporate promoter of African entertainment and sports. Glo flooded the creative industry with record-breaking sponsorship deals and endorsements, signing Nollywood legends, musical powerhouses, and sports heroes as brand ambassadors. From sponsoring the prestigious CAF African Footballer of the Year Awards and the Nigerian Premier League to funding cultural festivals, comedy tours, and reality shows, Glo actively elevated African talent to global prominence. Through these cultural investments, the brand cultivated an emotional connection with millions of subscribers, proving that an African brand could stand tall, celebrate its heritage, and deliver world-class service without losing its soul. Industry analysts frequently cite Globacom as more than just a corporate success; it is an enduring case study in what happens when visionary local leadership is matched with long-term capital and solid determination. Over 23 years, Glo has weathered fierce market competition, rapid technological transitions from 2G to 5G, and volatile macroeconomic shifts, all while maintaining its position at the top tier of African telecommunications. As customers, industry leaders, and well-wishers celebrate GLO@23, the milestone serves as a powerful tribute to a titan who dared to build on his own terms. Today, Globacom isn’t merely a telecom network; it stands as living proof of African capability, self-determination, and industrial excellence. As the green network prepares for its next era of digital expansion, artificial intelligence integration, and next-generation connectivity, one truth remains crystal clear across Africa’s business landscape: The Bull is still on the throne, and his legacy is built to last. Bodex Hungbo, a media professional, writes from Lagos. The post GLO@23: The Bull still reigns supreme appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: A black face and a thousand ships, by Bisi Adeleye-Fayemi
items.description: We read Homer’s ‘The Odyssey’ when we were in school, about King Odysseus of Ithaca who joined other Kings in the Trojan war. It took King Odysseus ten long years to make it back home to Ithaca. We remember the captivating, epic story of love, honour, betrayal, loyalty and redemption. The adventures of King Odysseus began with the narrative of ‘the face that launched a thousand ships’. Helen of Troy was known in Greek mythology as the most beautiful woman in the world. She was the daughter of the God Zeus and Leda. Many Greek Kings wanted her, and she ended up with King Menelaus of Sparta. The myth was not clear if Helen fell in love with the visiting Trojan Prince Paris and eloped with him, or if he kidnapped her. What is without doubt is the rage of her husband and his determination to get her back. A massive Greek fleet was assembled by King Menelaus and his allies, and they proceeded to lay siege on Troy. Reading Homer’s ‘The lliad’, as a child who was being educated in a post-colonial, commonwealth country, it is no surprise that right from the time I learnt about these characters, the image of Helen of Troy was one of a white woman. Who else would have a face that could launch a thousand ships? When Hollywood produced the Cleopatra epic in 1963, there was no outrage, when Elizabeth Taylor was cast as Cleopatra. Cleopatra existed for real, she was not a mythical character like Helen of Troy, yet the most acceptable face to portray her was a Caucasian actress. In 2004, Wolfgang Peterson produced Troy, which was an all-star mega production. According to reports, famous actresses such as Nicole Kidman and Uma Thurman were considered for the role of Helen. Wolfgang Peterson, who was also the Director, insisted on throwing it open to a global search that involved thousands of candidates. He settled for the German actress Diane Kruger who met all the boxes he had in mind. Knowing Hollywood standard operating procedures, it was clear that whether famous or unknown, the ‘face that launched a thousand ships’ would be a white one. Till Christopher Nolan came along. In July 2026, The Odyssey was released to mixed reviews. While many acclaim the story-telling, cinematography and acting, the film is going to be best known for the casting choices of the Director, Christopher Nolan. The casting of Lupita Nyong’O as Helen of Troy has inspired reactions ranging from shock to disbelief and even disgust. Helen of Troy was the daughter of a God, her beauty was incomparable, she was so desirable that Kings fought for her and over her for years. Her face placed a thousand ships on the sea. That face, as literature, history, popular culture and convention has tried to tell us over the years, was definitely one that met global beauty standards. A face with the right skin tone, cheek bones, eyes, nose, neck. A body with all the right proportions. A woman who could be described as a Goddess. The image that Helen Kruger famously embodied when she played the role in 2004. In essence, what the reactions to Lupita Nyong’O’s casting as Helen of Troy tells us is that a black woman can never be beautiful enough to force Kings to go to war. Christopher Nolan could have chosen to cast any other actress of colour. He had many choices which included Latina, Asian and light skinned black women, with famous names from all those communities. Yet, he chose Lupita Nyong’O, a woman who is ‘unarguably black’. An Oscar and Daytime Emmy award winner. A woman from the African continent, who has distinguished herself as a film and stage actress. A model, producer, philanthropist and social justice advocate. What was Christopher Nolan trying to say with his casting of Lupita? He has not said why, he does not need to defend his choice. His attitude seems to be ‘Why not?’ We can attempt to read between the lines. Christopher Nolan’s agenda might have been to generate controversy. Controversy means attention and it is all good for ticket sales. However, the meaning I choose to give his choice is, ‘Who defines what beauty is? Who sets the standards? Who makes the rules?’ Too many times, we have been told and shown, what ‘beauty’ looks like. Beauty is tall, fair-skinned, slim, straight nose, long and wavy hair. There was a time when I thought we had overcome this narrative and had started to affirm the wholistic beauty of black women. Sadly, looking at the reactions to Lupita’s role as Helen of Troy, and seeing what is happening with many young women of colour, particularly African women, this battle is far from over. Right from the times of slavery when the shade of your skin determined if you would spend your life working in the fields or in the Master’s house, black women have suffered the consequences of falling within or without the established beauty standards. In some of our communities, being plump with ‘front and back endowments’ were acceptable beauty norms. Trust patriarchy to capitalize on this. For those born without, the savvy producers of artificial breasts, hips and backsides now do brisk business. What the manufacturers of these contraptions cannot do, medical procedures can take it from there. We now even have artificial pubic hair! So, we see young women struggling to invest resources trying to live up to these questionable standards of beauty. In the process, they not only endanger their health, they internalise all the negative stereotypes about how low black women are on the beauty hierarchy. The beauty industry has lived off our insecurities for too long. Fixations on skinny bodies, large, firm breasts, small waists, firm behinds, skin bleaching, expensive wigs, make-up that is unsuitable for all skintones, dubious skin-care products, we have had too much of this shoved down our throats. Beauty is universal, and so it makes sense that expressions of beauty are everywhere, regardless of race, ethnicity, body size, hair texture and skin tone. Recently, Naomie Pilula, a Lawyer from Zambia, posted a selfie of herself. It went viral, with astonishing comments about how ugly she was, the level of cyber-bullying was terrible. Naomie, however, proceeded to teach her detractors a powerful lesson. She not only refused to take her photograph down, she stated that she knows she might not fit conventional beauty standards, but she loves herself and embraces her unique appearance. Naomie went from being a laughingstock because of her ‘lack of beauty’ to commanding respect due to her integrity. In 2026, thanks to Christopher Nolan, when we think about ‘a face that launched a thousand ships’, the image that comes to mind should not automatically be that of a blue-eyed, blond, model-thin Caucasian woman. Who is a beautiful woman? Lupita Nyong’O is a resilient, dignified, well-educated, award-winning, talented woman. A worthy role model, whose beauty is internal as well as external. Let us encourage our daughters to seek self-love like Lupita and Naomie, and support them to make affirming choices. Let them grow to be proud of whatever size or shade they are. They should know that they are worthy and they are enough. They should have power and control over their image on their own terms, and not because they believe this is what men want. Many men don’t even know what they want. People should stop calling light-skinned women ‘clean’ and dark-skinned women, ‘dirty’. It is appalling and makes us no better than our then slave masters. No woman should be made to feel that she is too ugly or unattractive for the world she lives in. Who determines that? Is itthe men she will come across, many of who will likely look like they got run over by a bus? Not every man is a Denzel Washington, Idris Elba, Jude Bellingham or Maduka Okoye. Black women are beautiful. African women are beautiful. And Lupita Nyong’O? She is a Goddess whose face and body can launch a thousand missiles. The post A black face and a thousand ships, by Bisi Adeleye-Fayemi appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Put your wife down at your peril!
items.description: By Bunmi Sofola LARA had often moaned that someone else had got the life she was supposed to have. We were mates at the secondary school and have remained close decades after we left. A fairly brilliant student, we were all mildly surprised when she opted for matrimony. Within the spate of a decade, she’d not only had four children, she’d become fat and frumpy. It didn’t help that her husband’s clerical job didn’t pay much to keep the family above the breadline. In the end Lara resigned her low-paid job and trained as a caterer. “It was the best move I’d made so far,” Lara had said. “After running a modest canteen, I was extremely lucky when one of our mates in school helped me get the job of running the canteen in her office. It was a big one too and the responsibilities were challenging. But there were perks too – it meant the difference between paying the school fees and putting decent meals on the table. “You would think Lere my husband would appreciate the extra money. The business centre he set up when he was retrenched wasn’t bringing in much and that really frustrated him. When we argued, he said lots of things – that I didn’t know when to shut up, that I looked like the back of an elephant. He even complained I came home reeking of kitchen fume. “Thanks to his criticism, I spruced myself up a bit. I got some new clothes I could afford and tried applying make-up. The staff teased me but I enjoyed the attention. But the day that really changed my life for the better happened some nine months ago. We were already packing up for the day when one of the top officials sent for me. He was going to work late and wondered if I could rustle up something for him to eat. I told him I would try my best. The rest of the canteen staff were all set to leave, so I told them not to bother, I would handle things. When I later took the tray to the man, we shall call him Leo, he was already on the settee in his office with a lot of files on the coffee table. I cleared a portion of the table and set the food down. I gave him drinks from his fridge and told him I would wait at the reception when he was through. He shook his head and told me to sit with him as he ate. He told me to help myself to a drink and I took a bottle of stout. He raised his brow slightly and giggled. When I sat next to him again, I noticed a photo of three smiling children – all boys and they looked just like him. He chatted as he had his meal and I realised what friendly man he was. “The setting was so domesticated that I suddenly realised I missed proper sex and felt sexually drawn to Leo. I don’t know where the courage came from but as he raised his glass for more drinks, I leant forward and kissed him. Leo’s eyes widened in surprise. I thought he might recoil, embarrassed, and order me out of his office. Instead, he pulled me closer and frantically kissed me back. As he pushed my top up, I tugged at his trousers. His fingers were all over my boobs. I was wearing an old, grey bra, but he didn’t mind. He pushed it up, wanting skin to skin. Some of the files laid scattered on the floor but we took no notice. I ended up with some of them under my buttocks as we made frantic love. I felt I was that ‘someone else’, that I had finally taken my life back. When it was over, Leo seemed happy with himself as he gave me a cuddle. ‘You’re one sexy big girl!’ he whispered. In that moment, I knew it would has. Sex with my husband had become something that happened on a Saturday night when he rolled in from his beer parlour to wake me up. I missed proper sex and thank goodness, Leo is providing that. “I supposed you could say we’re having an affair – except that Leo and I never meet anywhere but at the office. Yet it’s enough for me. Lere and I are still arguing. A few nights ago, I even blurted out in the heat of temper: ‘I’m sleeping with one of my bosses!’ He looked at me as if I’d gone off my senses. ‘Don’t be daft,’ he snorted. ‘Who’d want a fat slob like you?’ Well, Leo does. And that’s why I won’t stop what I’m doing. I can face life and my husband’s callous indifference as long as Leo wants me. He’s a very generous man too. Come to think of it, I must be a lot cheaper than those hoity-toity high-maintenance girls in the office – and I’m no threat. “Thanks to his generosity, I’m able to afford small luxuries for the family – including my husband! I’ve shed a bit of weight too – not that much as I enjoy my food. If Lere notices anything, he hasn’t said a word. He should really be grateful that another man is helping him shoulder his responsibilities. Sweet Smell Of Success! (Humour) Sitting at home one night with his wife, a man is casually tossing peanuts into the air and catching them in his mouth. As the couple take in the latest episode of watchdog, the man loses concentration for a split second and a peanut goes into his ear. He tries to get the nut out, but succeeds only in forcing the thing in awfully deep. After a few hours of fruitless rooting, the couple decide to go to the hospital, but on their way out of the front door they met their daughter coming in with her boyfriend. The boyfriend takes control of the situation: he tell them he’s studying medicine and that they’re not to worry about a thing. He then sticks two fingers up the man’s nose and asks him to blow – and lo, the nut shoots from the ear and out across the room. As the daughter and her boy friend go through the kitchen to make a pot of tea, the man and his wife sit down to discuss their luck. “So, the wife says,” what do you think he’ll become after he qualifies? A GP or a surgeon?” “Well,” says the man, rubbing his nose, “by the smell of his fingers, our son-in-law.” In The Heat Of Passion A man and his wife are driving home in their expensive new car one night when they both got horny, and decided to christen the sparkling motor with a shag. Pulling into a lay-by they get down to business, but soon realise their nice new motor’s actually too small for the amount of erotic manoeuvring they want to do. The guy suggests they limb out and have a go under the car, which he promises his wife will provide ample clearance for his heavy buttocks, so the couple slip under the pristine vehicle and go at it like the clappers. In fact, they’re enjoying themselves so much that they don’t notice when a policeman comes over and taps the man on the back of his exposed legs. “What do you think you’re doing?” the copper asks the man. “I’m fixing my car,” the chap calmly replies. “No you’re not!” the policeman says through hysterical laughter. “You’re having sex in public, and, I’m going to nick you for indecent exposure.” “How do you know I’m lying?” the indignant man asks. “Well,” the copper replies, “for a start, you’re facing downwards on top of a naked woman. Secondly, I don’t see any tools anywhere. And thirdly, your car was stolen five minutes ago.” The post Put your wife down at your peril! appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Déficit de magistrats en Guinée : « moins de 500 magistrats pour plus de 17 millions d’habitants »(ministre de la Justice)
items.description: Le déficit de magistrats constitue toujours un défi majeur pour le système judiciaire guinéen. Le constat a été une nouvelle fois dressé ce samedi 8 août 2026 par le Garde des Sceaux, ministre de la Justice et des Droits de l’homme, à l’occasion du lancement du concours de recrutement de futurs magistrats. Pour Ibrahima Sory 2 Tounkara, les effectifs actuels de la magistrature sont largement insuffisants au regard du poids démographique du pays. La Guinée compte aujourd’hui moins de 500 magistrats pour une population estimée à 17,6 millions d’habitants, selon les données avancées par le ministre. « La justice guinéenne a un manque criard de magistrats. Et ce vide-là, il faut qu'on le comble. Aujourd'hui, on a moins de 500 magistrats en République de Guinée pour une population estimée aujourd'hui à 17 600 000 », a-t-il alerté. Pour illustrer l’ampleur du déficit, le Garde des Sceaux a mis en avant l’écart entre le ratio recommandé et la situation actuelle de la Guinée. Selon lui, alors que les normes internationales préconisent un magistrat pour 10 000 habitants, le pays en compte actuellement un pour environ 42 000 personnes. Une disparité qu’il juge particulièrement préoccupante : « Quand vous regardez le ratio, les normes internationales reconnaissent un magistrat aujourd'hui pour 10 000 habitants. Et nous, si vous calculez le nombre de magistrats aujourd'hui par rapport au nombre de la population, vous trouverez qu'il y a un magistrat pour 42 000 personnes. Vous voyez maintenant la disparité ? Donc c'est pourquoi il nous faut encore recruter beaucoup de magistrats », a-t-il alerté à travers un reportage diffusé sur la télévision nationale. Pour cette session de recrutement, 766 candidats ont été autorisés à concourir. Après les différentes phases de sélection et d’évaluation, le jury devra retenir 100 candidats, appelés à intégrer la magistrature au terme du processus de formation prévu à cet effet.

items.title: NaCCA warns schools against use of unapproved assessment materials
items.description: The National Council for Curriculum and Assessment (NaCCA) has directed all pre-tertiary schools across the country to stop using assessment items and mock examination papers that have not been vetted and approved by the Council. The directive, contained in a public notice dated August 7, 2026, follows what NaCCA described as the continued use of assessment items and mock examinations developed by unapproved assessment consultancies, institutions and individuals in some basic schools. The notice was signed by the Director-General of NaCCA, Prof. Samuel Ofori Bekoe. NaCCA, the statutory body mandated to approve assessment items and tasks for pre-tertiary schools in Ghana, said no school was permitted to administer externally developed assessment materials unless they had first been vetted and approved by the Council. “All heads of pre-tertiary schools are directed to comply with this directive with immediate effect,” the notice stated. The Council warned that schools that procure, administer or facilitate the use of unapproved assessment materials would be liable to appropriate regulatory sanctions. NaCCA raises concern over assessment quality The directive is intended to ensure that assessment materials used in schools conform to approved curriculum and assessment standards and maintain consistency in the evaluation of learners. NaCCA expressed concern over the growing practice of schools relying on assessment materials produced by external entities without the Council’s approval. The Council stressed that its statutory mandate includes the approval of assessment items and tasks for pre-tertiary education, making its vetting process an important requirement before such materials are administered to pupils. The latest directive therefore places responsibility on heads of pre-tertiary institutions to ensure that all externally developed assessment materials have received the necessary approval before they are used. NaCCA further cautioned schools against procuring or facilitating the use of materials that have not gone through the prescribed approval process, warning that such conduct could attract regulatory action. The directive covers assessment items and mock examination papers used in pre-tertiary schools, including basic schools.
