items.title: Osun 2026: Between politics and law, by Tonnie Iredia
items.description: The matter of the moment in the last couple of days has been the rift between the Osun state government and the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission EFCC. While Nigerians have continued to comment on the subject, a major gain of the nation is the people’s realization that if their president is careful and observant, he can easily become personally conscious of public opinion. President Bola Ahmed Tinubu passed that simple exam of the week by intervening in the EFCC-Osun rift. The strategic intervention has not only soaked the political tension in Osun; it has dramatically converted the tension into a debate for all comers sending political jobbers back to the drawing board to find new controversies to create. Tinubu must take advantage of the gain by staying away from relying on only the version of a story told by allies, aides and supporters. For each controversy, a leader must seek to comprehend all the dimensions of the stories he is told. Before Tinubu, a few presidents relied on the one-sided story at the expense of their image. For example, President Jonathan should not have relied entirely on a supposed technical advice to change his plan to personally visit Chibok. If a president who is armed to the teeth is dissuaded by men of technical and security expertise from visiting a troubled spot, what does he expect the public to feel and into what use is he expected to put his gamut of security convoy? We submit that there is always a difference between technicality, law and politics. It is against this backdrop that the decision of President Tinubu to put a pause on EFCC’s action in Osun state ought to be interrogated. I have watched many colleagues on national television marshalling several points to disagree with the intervention. Some of their arguments especially the legal options they have raised are no doubt quite persuasive but President Tinubu’s intervention was not designed to deal with a legal topic. The argument that he should have left the matter to his Attorney General establishes clearly that the commentators had made up their minds that it is only through law that matters are resolved which is not true. I want to believe that whereas the commentators were looking at the letters of the law, the president was thinking of the spirit of the law. Law to my mind is useless if its handling cannot prevent the dismemberment of society. Those of us who think Tinubu’s intervention was not bad are not in any way suggesting that EFCC was pursuing any hidden or illegal agenda. Indeed, we are strong among those who have found cause to commend the current leadership of that reformed anti-corruption agency. So much has changed there; prosecution has improved, convictions have increased while it has embraced an effective inter-agency synergy that is yielding great positive results. We also agree with the argument that the EFCC was acting within its legal mandate in its Osun mission. The point to be made therefore is that it is simplistic to see the president’s intervention as evidence that the EFCC did some wrong. What appears to have unsettled the president was not EFCC’s work but the public opinion that the agency was being used to destabilize a sitting state government so as to empower the political party of the president to take over the state. Almost every Nigerian believes this which the state concerned has helped to amplify across all digital media organs. Even the EFCC would be shocked to learn that some of its staff do not only feel so but may have confirmed it privately to their friends and family. What this suggests is that most people must have imagined that it was the president who may have directed the EFCC to do the hatchet job on Osun state especially as he was quoted to have said recently that all is fair in politics. With only a few months away to his own re-election bid, there is no way Tinubu would have adopted the option of ‘silence is golden’ and allow the damaging public opinion to take root. The president actually has many more interventions to make to reduce the unduly high degree of politicisation of Nigeria. In the last decade, the only industry flourishing in our country is politics. It has become so attractive that people are prepared to kill to get into office. Painfully, threats are carried out using the privileges of public office. Members of the ruling party at the national level are usually able to access the instruments of coercion to perpetrate violence. The president must therefore intervene to halt the trend whereby people in government often seek to overwhelm members of the opposition. That is not democracy It is worse when the opposition in a state such as Osun is seen by the public as strong enough to overpower a state government – a development that is likely to happen only through the help of federal power. If the same overpowering opposition party in a state wins the next election, no one is likely to believe that it was through the ballot. There is therefore no better time than now for President Tinubu to put a halt to the belligerence in Osun or any such state. The idea of a ruling party losing at the polls happens all over the world. But it usually happens when an opposition has better ideas or more charismatic candidates who are able to persuade voters. It is time to stop the victories attained in our clime through the force of law or fraudulent systems. In particular, let’s stop the show of force in the states by Abuja-based politicians. Perhaps, one way of doing this is to alter our attitude to elections. About a decade ago when the current ruling APC was in the opposition, it went to court to stop the use of the military in our elections. The court ruled in its favour; yet, the involvement of the military in elections in Nigeria is increasing. Who usually approves the release of the military to our election merchants and into what use do they put them? Why do we require soldiers to be part of our elections when we keep saying the worst democratic government is better than the best military dictatorship? Is our election so tense that we need more than the Police? Is it not strange that security agencies are even more active in non-chaotic segments like collation of votes? Answers to the above posers may help us understand the direction of the Osun governorship election which is just a few days away. For me, as an independent election observer, I will always remember the Osun Governorship election which took place on Saturday, September 22, 2018. The current governor, Ademola Adeleke was also the leading candidate at the time but INEC refused to declare him the winner because of certain issues in about 7 polling units. According to the electoral body, the election was inconclusive – a popular title at the time, so a rerun was fixed for Thursday September 27, 2018. During the rerun which INEC announced was won by the ruling party rather than the leading candidate, both voters and election observers were harassed by security agencies to achieve a predetermined goal. The US, EU and UK observers reported irregularities and interference by inappropriate persons in the election. As we are set to re-enact the old 19th Century battle of Osogbo 1840, there is need to caution politicians to let the contest be determined by voters rather than by top politicians who would converge on the state to ensure their party wins by whatever method. If that is allowed, it would be a bigger stain to wash than stopping the EFCC that would have evidence to justify its actions. This is why we call on the President today to take the same step he took concerning the EFCC to warn INEC to be diligent in handling the coming Osun election. He should also send a strong appeal to his own party members especially their “inter-state professional players” to allow Osun APC members run the show in line with the rules set for the game. A ruling party is usually a big party with all manner of members – wealthy chieftains, gentlemen, fraudsters etc. In its days, PDP had specialized riggers, most of whom have since defected to their successor party. Whoever can counsel such riggers to allow us have credible election would have done so much service to the fatherland. This is because it is only from credible elections that we can source visionary leaders who would formulate and implement proactive public policies that can improve the living conditions of our compatriots and push Nigeria into the big league of developed political entities. The post Osun 2026: Between politics and law, by Tonnie Iredia appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Obasanjo, Osoba, AD, and 2003 old men stale stuff, by Dele Sobowale
items.description: “The loser at the hazard, when the game breaks up/ Sadder, sorrier lingers on alone Replays each throw and drinks of wisdom’s cup” – Aligheri Dante, 1265-1321, in Purgatory. For me, this is one of the most painful articles I have ever had to write in 39 years of writing for VANGUARD. In a fight between older brothers, friends and political associates on the one hand, and, a barely tolerable opponent on the other side, I naturally stand by the former – and damn the consequences. This is the first exception. With all due respects to my senior brothers in the South-West, the recent controversy between former President Obasanjo and former Governor Osoba, can most aptly be regarded as “the same stale old stew, warmed up and served in new plates” (Apologies to ex-President Babangida). Nothing substantially new was added to what we knew already before the fresh outburst. I know why we are again being treated to another round of recriminations. I will discuss that later. I was never a party card holder; but, my family had been in the progressive camp ever since my eldest brother, the late Chief Sanu Sobowale, joined the Action Group Youth Wing with the late Chief Bola Ige. I had the privilege of knowing Ige when he and my brother attended Ibadan Grammar School. Ige was the Kaduna Boy; my brother was the Zaria Boy in their class. They exchanged visits and that was when I first came across the man later nicknamed Cicero. I remember, as if it happened yesterday, my encounter with the late Chief Ayo Adebanjo; lifetime stalwart of Afenifere, in his chambers at the Western House, Broad Street, Lagos Island. I was sitting watching the NTA News, for days before the meeting, when it was reported that the leaders of AD/Afenifere had reached an agreement with President Obasanjo not to field a presidential candidate for the 2003 elections. Despite the fact that Nigeria and the world were still several years from when government-controlled media agencies broadcast barefaced lies, the announcement was still incredible to me; principally, because it made no sense for AD. REQUIEM FOR AD/AFENIFERE “To know/That which before us lies in daily life/Is the prime wisdom, what is more is fume” – John Milton, 1608-1674, VANGUARD BOOK OF QUOTATIONS p 275 There was only one way to find out. I wrote an article the Sunday after the announcement titled REQUIEM FOR AD. Briefly summarized, my position was this: First, given the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria, the presidency is the only position any political party should aspire to hold. My political arithmetic convinced me that, unlike the US Constitution, the Nigerian president had more clout than all the 36 governors combined. Any party not vying for the presidency is heading for the graveyard of politics. Second, AD/Afenifere controlling the six states of the South West should aim at expanding its influence nationwide, while still contesting for president; and hope that superior governance in the zone would attract support from other states. Third, and this was perhaps the most important, Obasanjo should not be trusted, the agreement announced sounded to me like the lion asking the leopard to form a hunting partnership; every success to be shared equally. The leopard might soon find itself on the lion’s menu. Fourth, I ended by asking the leaders of AD/Afenifere to withdraw from the deal. That was the main presentation – which characteristically was full of global precedents as well as one of local examples. The article appeared on Sunday; I received an urgent message from the late Chief Ayo Adebanjo, highly respected, almost worshipped, who I visited several times before. It was a most unhappy meeting for both of us. The late Chief Adebanjo, like most great men, sooner or later, invest themselves with infallibility. They can never be wrong; and they don’t tolerate younger people trying to correct them; more so, when it was a group decision made by older, more experienced politicians and wiser than me. He proceeded to lecture me on the details of the agreement. The more he revealed, the more alarmed I became. I couldn’t believe that our most trusted leaders in the progressive alliance could be so easily duped. The meeting turned combative when I asked a question. “Sir, you said Obasanjo agreed to leave your governors untouched. What if he reneges on that promise? It will be too late to make amends.” “Obasanjo is a senior military officer; they keep their words.” “Sir, that is precisely my fear. Deception is fair in war; and politics is like war without shooting.” “Are you saying that the president of Nigeria can be distrusted?” “Yes Sir, on a matter like this.” “Dele, please walk out of my office.” Unfortunately for the progressives, the leaders had been lured to their own self-destruction. One victim of this catastrophe was of particular interest to me. SEGUN OSOBA, OLD BOY, METHODIST BOYS HIGH SCHOOL, LAGOS “God save me from my friends; I can take care of my enemies.” Senior Segun Osoba and I grew up in Lagos; he was my senior at Methodist Boys High School while I was trailing a few years behind at Igbobi College. Both schools valued high ethical standards and bred them into the students. He was unprepared for politics. Lagos boys always were instinctive loyal to each other. I was totally devoted to Osoba; I also feared for his safety given the agreement with Obasanjo. Chief Osoba, like all politicians, had enemies; who never hurt him. Instead, he was a victim of his friends in AD/Afenifere as well as his newly found “friend” – President Obasanjo. As soon as the pact was sealed, Osoba could be seen at the Lagos Airport to receive the president each time Obasanjo was in Lagos and Abeokuta. The governor was faithful to the terms of the deal; the president was not. It was painful watching the game playing out; though I naively thought that Osoba would defeat anybody thrown at him; deal or not. I was at the VANGUARD Editorial meeting the day Gbenga Daniel came to announce his candidacy for the governorship of Ogun State. We listened politely and laughed heartily when he departed. To us, it was a bloody joke for anybody to want to challenge Osoba. Complacency crept in; Osoba hardly campaigned. I cried when the results came in; Osoba and four other AD governors had been sent home. The deception had worked as I predicted. Chief Adebanjo and I met, at a funeral, months after the AD/Afenifere had lost five states, leaving only Lagos State; where Bola Tinubu had refused to be a party to the agreement. Good upbringing demanded that I should greet first and respectfully. It was not triumph but sadness. The progressive movement in the South-West had been decapitated. Henceforth, the zone will fall into the hands of non-Awoists. PLEASE STOP THE NEEDLESS CONTROVERSY “A peaceful mind is often built by avoiding arguments that prove nothing” – Author Unknown Just as I was struggling with how to end this article, stopping at a petrol station yielded this gem of advice on the back of a T-shirt worn by a bus driver. I quickly wrote it down. The current controversy erupted when someone pointed to references made in Osoba’s book concerning the 2003 elections. Obasanjo was portrayed as a traitor. Ever combative and deeply self-righteous, Baba Iyabo rejected the branding. As far as he was concerned, he played higher level politics and won handsomely. The losers are still licking their wounds. Nothing to apologise for. This is a classic case of a dispute involving parties who cannot even agree on what the disagreement is all about. Under the circumstances, my modest proposal to both sides is for them to stop this needless controversy. AD/Afenifere committed a monumental blunder; which swept them away as a political force. Obasanjo, military, took advantage of their innocence; and is not magnanimous in victory. Nothing more will be gained by disputes. We are bored. OBASANJO: HOW NOT TO BE A RESPECTED ELDER STATESMAN “Character is destiny.” Obasanjo versus Fayose, Obasanjo versus Osoba, Obasanjo versus Atiku…and the list goes on. Each and every time former President Obasanjo exchanges insults with those less divinely blessed than he, the old man diminishes himself more. A man, who should be above political fray; who should enjoy, indeed command, the respect of all Nigerians, routinely collects insults like a pig in polluted marshland. It is a pity that one of our human national monuments willfully debases the institution of past presidents. It was disclosed in his altercation with Fayose that N10 million had been sent to him together with invitation – before disagreements occurred and insults were exchanged. “I clothed and fed you, Atiku fires back at Obasanjo” – VANGUARD, August 2, 2026 Any man with self-respect does not invite people to wash his dirty underwear in public. Why is Obasanjo doing this to himself? The man is his own worst enemy… •Follow me on Facebook @ J Israel Biola The post Obasanjo, Osoba, AD, and 2003 old men stale stuff, by Dele Sobowale appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Mamou : le ministre de la Culture annonce des funérailles nationales pour l’Almamy Bocar Biro
items.description: En visite à Mamou ce samedi 8 août 2026, le ministre de la Culture, du Tourisme et de l’Artisanat, Moussa Moïse Sylla, a annoncé que des funérailles nationales seront organisées en l’honneur de l’Almamy Bocar Biro Barry et de ses compagnons, si la France accepte de restituer leurs crânes réclamés officiellement par la Guinée. Depuis l’annonce de la demande officielle de restitution adressée à la France, le débat anime l’opinion à Mamou. La Guinée souhaite récupérer les crânes de l’Almamy Bocar Biro Barry, de son fils Modi Sory, de son frère Thierno Ciré et de son chef de guerre Satigui Modou, conservés au Musée de l’Homme à Paris. À Mamou, les avis sont partagés sur le sort qui devrait être réservé à ces reliques historiques. Certains souhaitent leur conservation dans un musée afin de permettre aux générations futures et aux visiteurs de découvrir l’histoire de l’Almamy Bocar Biro. D’autres estiment qu’ils doivent être inhumés auprès des restes de leurs corps, conformément aux coutumes et aux traditions. Face aux populations et aux sages réunis à l’occasion du lancement des travaux de la construction du musée regional de Mamou, le ministre de la Culture, Moussa Moïse Sylla, a apporté une réponse claire à cette question. « Almamy Bocar Biro, dernier souverain de l’État théocratique du Foutah, opposa en 1896 une résistance héroïque et farouche à la pénétration coloniale française. 130 ans plus tard, sous le leadership du président Mamadi Doumbouya, nous sommes sur la voie de réhabiliter l’Almamy Bocar Biro », a-t-il déclaré. Le ministre a rappelé que la Guinée a officiellement saisi la France pour demander la restitution des quatre reliques. « Au nom du président de la République, nous avons fait un courrier officiel pour demander à la France de nous retourner les quatre reliques. Donc, ce n’est pas pour venir les exposer dans un musée ici », a précisé Moussa Moïse Sylla. Selon lui, la décision est déjà arrêtée au plus haut niveau de l’État. En cas de réponse favorable de la France, la Guinée entend organiser des funérailles nationales en hommage à l’Almamy Bocar Biro et à ses compagnons. « Dès que la demande va avoir une réponse positive, sur les instructions du président de la République, nous allons organiser des funérailles nationales à l’honneur de l’Almamy Bocar Biro et faire en sorte qu’ils soient enterrés, lui et ses compagnons », a annoncé le ministre. Cette démarche s’inscrit, selon Moussa Moïse Sylla, dans une volonté plus large de réhabiliter les figures historiques ayant résisté à la colonisation et contribué à forger l’identité et la dignité du peuple guinéen. « Tous nos héros qui ont défendu et qui ont fait de la Guinée un pays de résistance et de dignité, qu’on puisse les réhabiliter », a-t-il conclu. La restitution de ces quatre reliques, si elle est acceptée par la France, ouvrirait ainsi une nouvelle page dans la mémoire historique de la Guinée et pourrait donner lieu à une cérémonie nationale dédiée à l’un des derniers grands souverains du Foutah Djallon.

items.title: Alerte sur la RN1 : un embouteillage monstre à Labota après le renversement d’un camion
items.description: Un camion renversé sur la chaussée provoque, ce samedi 8 août 2026, un important embouteillage à Labota, paralysant la circulation sur la RN1. La situation est également aggravée par deux autres accidents signalés en direction de Kindia, peu avant Débélé, perturbant fortement le trafic sur cet axe très fréquenté « La situation est vraiment difficile. Nous sommes bloqués depuis un bon moment et la circulation n’avance presque pas. Il faut renforcer les contrôles et sanctionner sévèrement les chauffeurs qui mettent en danger la vie des usagers », témoigne un conducteur bloqué dans les embouteillages. Un autre usager appelle à une réaction urgente des autorités « Après le récent drame de Labota qui a fait sept morts, voir encore des accidents sur cet axe est très inquiétant. Les autorités doivent prendre des mesures urgentes pour sécuriser cette route et éviter d’autres pertes en vies humaines. » a-t-il rappelé. Face à la répétition des accidents sur la RN1 Conakry-Kindia, les usagers appellent les autorités à renforcer les contrôles, à sanctionner les comportements dangereux et à prendre des mesures concrètes pour améliorer la sécurité routière sur cet axe.

items.title: Belgique : la Pro League démarre sa nouvelle saison sous un nouveau format
items.description: Le championnat belge de football de première division (Pro League) a démarré cette fin de semaine sa nouvelle saison 2026/27, avec un nouveau format marqué par un retour à une compétition classique à 18 équipes et l’abandon des Playoffs, pour la première fois depuis 2008/09. L’élargissement du championnat à 18 équipes, au lieu de 16, implique un match de plus par journée, pour un total de 34 journées, et il y aura cinq tickets européens à se partager à l’issue de la saison, sans passer par des matchs de barrage, selon les nouvelles règles annoncées par la ligue de football professionnel belge. Ainsi, le champion de Belgique sera automatiquement qualifié pour la phase de ligue de la Ligue des champions, alors que le vice-champion passera par les tours éliminatoires de la C1. Le vainqueur de la Coupe sera qualifié, quant à lui, pour les barrages de l’Europa League, et le troisième du championnat sera envoyé au deuxième tour préliminaire de cette compétition. Enfin, le quatrième du championnat ira au deuxième tour préliminaire de la Conférence League. Par ailleurs, les deux dernières équipes du classement, les 17e et 18e, descendent en Challenger Pro League, la deuxième division du football belge, également appelée la D1B. Le champion et le vainqueur des barrages de promotion entre les équipes classées 2e, 3e, 4e et 5e de la D1B sont promus en Pro League. En outre, de nouvelles règles entrent en vigueur dans les matchs du championnat. Le VAR aura notamment la possibilité d’intervenir dans de nouveaux cas de figure : Lorsqu’un corner a été attribué par erreur, les arbitres vidéo devront le signaler à l’arbitre principal, et le VAR pourra également désormais intervenir en cas de carton jaune entraînant une exclusion ou d’erreur sur l’identité du joueur averti. La chasse au gain de temps est l’autre grand objectif des adaptations du règlement: les changements, les blessures, mais aussi les touches et les coups de pied de but seront scrutés de près par les arbitres. La saison 2026/27 de la Pro League devrait prendre fin le 21 mai 2027, alors que la finale de la coupe de Belgique devrait avoir lieu le 30 mai 2027, pour renouer avec la tradition faisant de ce match le dernier rendez-vous du football belge de la saison. items.title: NAN institutionalises quarterly fitness walks to boost staff wellness, productivity
items.description: By Henry Obetta The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN), Lagos Directorate, in collaboration with Alpha Designs Nigeria Ltd., on Saturday organised its maiden fitness walk for staff as part of efforts to promote healthy living, physical fitness and improved workplace productivity. The programme, which brought together members of staff and other participants, featured a walk from the Teslim Balogun Stadium to the NAN Lagos office, alongside physical exercises and other wellness activities. Speaking at the event, Managing Director of NAN, Malam Ali Mohammed Ali, said the initiative was designed to encourage staff to pay greater attention to their physical wellbeing, stressing that a healthy workforce was essential to effective service delivery. Ali said wellness and fitness had become an integral part of NAN’s workplace culture, noting that the agency had institutionalised quarterly fitness activities across its directorates. “Under our watch at NAN, wellness and fitness have become more than a slogan. It has become a quarterly tradition that we are proud to institutionalise across all our directorates. “Beyond these quarterly walks and jogs, we have also taken concrete steps to promote wellness in the workplace. “That is why, to protect and promote wellness at the agency, we have, in Abuja, twice every week, specifically on Tuesdays and Fridays, reduced the official work hours by one hour to enable staff to make use of our well-equipped gym at the Abuja headquarters. “This deliberate policy is to ensure that fitness becomes part of our daily culture, not just an occasional event,” he said. The NAN helmsman urged staff members to embrace physical fitness as a lifestyle rather than a quarterly activity, stressing that a sound mind and healthy body were essential to improved work performance and productivity. Deputy Editor-in-Chief and Head of Operations, NAN Lagos, Kevin Okunzuwa, who also served as Chairman of the Local Organising Committee for the fitness walk, said the programme provided an opportunity for media practitioners to prioritise their health, refresh physically and mentally, and strengthen bonds among colleagues. “The bottom line is that we should always endeavour to take care of ourselves. Our health matters a lot. “For whoever goes beyond this world, the job will always remain there for someone to take over,” he said. Also speaking, Business Development Personnel at Alpha Designs Nigeria Ltd., Onyeagbo Ugochi, said promoting healthy living remained a core objective of the organisation. Ugochi highlighted Alpha Designs’ newly launched wellness platform, Genesis New Vision App, designed to promote healthy living practices among members of the public, and urged Nigerians to download and use the application. She said the organisation’s sustained collaboration with NAN was aimed at encouraging Nigerians to become more intentional about their health as part of its corporate social responsibility initiative. Ugochi added that Alpha Designs remained open to collaborating with other organisations whose vision aligned with its commitment to promoting healthy living and wellness. Head of Lagos Operations, NAN, Ifeyinwa Omowole, also underscored the importance of taking responsibility for personal health, stressing that wellness was important not only for journalists but for everyone. “When you are healthy, you are fit to do your work, and we all know that journalism is a tasking work. “So, for you to be good at what you do, it is not just your brains; it is also your fitness,” she said. Omowole said the health talks delivered during the programme had further sensitised staff on practical ways to maintain fitness while working in the office. The event also featured health talks, raffle draws and cash rewards for participants. The post NAN institutionalises quarterly fitness walks to boost staff wellness, productivity appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Open SOS call to President Mahama for justice
items.description: Our elders have said it, owo ka aniberee meaning a snake bites or stings out of frustration or distress. The last time the Minister of Finance, Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, appeared in Parliament, he said, among other things, that there was no arrears and boasted that so much has been saved towards the settlement of the first batch of payments under the Domestic Debt Exchange Programme (DDEP), for which he was highly praised and applauded for the sound management of the economy. However, because the DDEP was used as a major political tool, the government is doing everything possible to meet commitments. But that is not the case for some ordinary Ghanaians, who instead of investing their finances in financial instruments or bonds, decided to supply food items under the Free Senior High School Policy in the Fourth Quarter of 2024. Because of our obsession with partisan politics, our simplistic understanding is that anybody who does business under a certain regime, willy nilly, is a member or fanatic supporter of the political party that is in control under that regime. However, it is a basic fact that not every such person is a political animal but a prudent individual who wants to deploy their finances prudently. More imperative, in our country, services and supplies for government business in the fourth quarter, are usually paid for in the First Quarter of the ensuing year. So, it happened that in September 2024, the Minister of Education, Dr Yaw Osei Adutwum, spoke to me personally to help supply maize to senior high schools in the Ashanti Region. He did so because most members of the Conference of Heads of Assisted Senior High Schools (CHASS) had recommended a company, Rostella Enterprise, as a dependent, committed and reliable supplier of domestic food items to the schools and the manageress of the company happened to be my wife. She was initially reluctant but I prevailed upon her, pointing out that the Free SHS programme is one of the most transformative policy initiatives of the government, whose full impact would be realised after more than a decade of implementation, when the literacy rate of the country is assessed. I also assured her that once it was a government project, payment could not be repudiated by any future government once it was established to be genuine. As a micro businesswoman, she had more discernment than myself, an innocent public servant who had an idealistic appreciation of our fundamentalist partisanship considerations. However, after much persuasion, she mobilised resources and supplied the food items. Her initial fears started to crystalise when the new government in 2025, decided to undertake a forensic audit into those supplies before going on with payments. Thankfully, the audit was concluded and in July last year, the President announced that all such outstanding payments were to resume. Both the National Food Buffer Stock Company and the Ghana Commodity Exchange, because of her record and the comments from members of CHASS in the Ashanti Region, encouraged her to register for new supplies, which she did by paying the respective registration fees of GHc5000 each. However, due to the infantile and puerile thinking that all such suppliers were partisan and loyal to the previous government she has not since been given a contract for supplies. When implementation commenced and allocations began, otherwise cooperative officials in both institutions became elusive and hostile to her enquires including a comment by one of the key officers at Buffer Stock, that he was not a member of the allocation committee and should not thus be disturbed any more. A few weeks back, she had assured that she was on the approval been list. This can only be a reflection of our warped thinking that those who get contracts under a government programme are loyalists or fanatical party supporters. The irony though is that when public, political and government officials get the opportunity to speak publicly, they openly proffer sentimental nationalistic slogans and regurgitate the false narration that the country belongs to all of us and no one would be excluded from the sharing of the national cake or resources and that government business is not based on nepotism nor partisanship but on competence, quality of work and value for money. Thus for the past 19 months the debt owed to Rostella Enterprise and others like her, whose only crime was that they did good business with the past administration, have had their money in arrears and each time they call to find out, the refrain is that we are waiting for releases from the Ministry of Finance. What is devilish is the fact that new suppliers appointed since 2025; ostensibly loyal partisan members of the government are paid from the Ghana Education Trust Fund. The question is, if government is raising money and depositing it towards the future payments under the DDEP, why has the same government failed to pay for supplies, forensically audited and established to be legitimate. What the hell is the difference between legitimate food supplied to Ghanaian senior secondary school students under the Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo regime and those supplied under President John Dramani Mahama, if not because of fanatical partisanship consideration. In an interview on Ghana Television last Tuesday, August 5, the Minister of Education, Haruna Iddrisu, my Law Class 2002 mate, pointed out that the uncapped portion of the GETFund, is being applied to pay for food supplies under the Free SHS programme. During the past administration, when suppliers under the same programme were owed and besieged the offices of Buffer Stock, it became justifiably a political matter and the Speaker of Parliament visited Buffer Stock to understand issues after which he appealed to the government to pay the suppliers, ordinary micro and small scale business men and women. It worked. For my part, when the Ministry of Education resorted to what was termed emergency supplies, which attracted prompt payments but cost higher, I complained directly to the Chief of Staff to draw her attention to the injustice and the travesty of the act, where those who had their supplies in arrears were paid less whilst emergency suppliers who were paid promptly received higher. She agreed with my submission that things bought on credit must cost more than those paid for instantly. Things began to work thereafter. Personally, what this government, through the Ministry of Finance has done to me is that, they have beaten me and compelled me from crying, but “anka wonua womu a yennyi wo mfiri mu.” It is simple. Beyond not paying my wife, as Chairman of the National Media Commission from 2018 to 2024, since the last Commission ended its tenure on December 24, 2024, we have not received our arrears for 2022, 2023 and 2024 although new members have been paid part of their allowance since they assumed duty in May 2025. The Minister of Finance and his colleagues who were MPs together with other Article 71 office holders have received their full salary arrears together with ex gratia awards whilst members of the NMC, the least remunerated among Article 71 office holders, are waiting endlessly for payment. Members of the NMC are unqualified for ex gratia because they are said to be part-time, although Council of State members, equally non-permanent, receive ex gratia, as per the denunciation made by Togbe Afede, against the lodgement of ex gratia money into his account some time ago. Whenever any of the former members of the NMC call me as Chairman to find out when the arrears would be paid, I call the accountant who keeps on telling me that they had not heard from the Ministry of Finance although the ministry collected the details for the payment in March 2025. Nsuo fono aponkyereni a ogye woo and more so, se kokoram amfere se obeto wo nan ho a wo nso wo mfere se wode asaawa anaa ntomago bekyekyere so. That is why I am openly appealing and reaching out to my former Roommate President John Dramani Mahama to ensure that justice is done to the previous NMC members, and more so, suppliers under the Free SHS programme, whose supplies have been in arrears since September 2024, knowing that it is the tradition of our country to meet outstanding payments from the Fourth Quarter in the First Quarter of the ensuing year, and especially because all funds sitting in the accounts of public agencies between January and March 2025 were swept back into the Consolidated Fund at the end of March as it is usual. By: Yaw Boadu Ayeboafo

items.title: FIFA condemns ‘concerted effort’ to weaken Infantino
items.description: FIFA on Saturday condemned “a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine” the world game’s governing body and its president Gianni Infantino as the controversy over his now shelved private investment plan rumbles on. Infantino has faced calls to resign and was also subject to allegations from a British newspaper on Friday that he paid off a lover while at European governing body UEFA. “Recent reporting has included unsubstantiated assertions and demonstrably false claims concerning FIFA and its President,” said the FIFA statement. Infantino served as secretary general of European football’s governing body from 2009 to 2016. According to The Telegraph newspaper, the Italian-Swiss lawyer previously used his influence to secure a promotion for a UEFA employee with whom he was in an intimate relationship. The newspaper added — without revealing its sources — that the same employee received a “a six-figure sum” upon her departure in addition to the payment of tuition fees for a business school amounting to around £45,000 ($60,700). When contacted by AFP, UEFA acknowledged that “a departure payment was made to the individual in question” at that time, “coupled with the payment of fees for an MBA course at a local business school”. – Growing pressure – In Saturday’s statement on social media, FIFA insisted it “welcomes legitimate scrutiny”. “But scrutiny is not a licence to distort facts, amplify unsubstantiated allegations or manufacture distractions designed to undermine progress. Where reporting is inaccurate or misleading, FIFA will challenge it directly and vigorously,” it added. Infantino, who is standing for re-election next March, has been embroiled in a crisis since the announcement late last month of his controversial — and ultimately abandoned — plan to open up the World Cup to private investors. He faces opposition in particular from UEFA, which on Thursday stood by its threat to boycott the World Cups, deeming the mere withdrawal of the controversial plan to be insufficient. FIFA said Saturday it “will not support, facilitate or tolerate any process concerning the election of the FIFA President that is inconsistent with FIFA’s Statutes, democratic procedures and established governance framework”. The statement added: “Those who do not have the support of FIFA’s Member Associations should not seek to achieve through allegation, insinuation or misinformation what they cannot achieve through FIFA’s established democratic processes.” AFP The post FIFA condemns ‘concerted effort’ to weaken Infantino appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 17 soldiers, others killed as buses collide in Niger
items.description: At least 22 people have died, 17 of them soldiers, after two buses crashed into each other in southern Niger, the West African country’s transport ministry said Saturday. The accident, a head-on collision between two buses, happened on Friday night some 50 kilometres (35 miles) from the town of Madaoua, said the ministry statement. Another 37 people were injured in the accident, it added. Earlier Saturday, the country’s official ANP news agency said one of the buses had been carrying soldiers and said an investigation into what caused the crash had been opened. This latest incident comes as the authorities campaign to raise awareness about the dangers of road accidents, a frequent occurrence on the vast Sahel nation’s roads. In 2025, Niger recorded more than 7,000 road accidents which killed over 1,200 people and left more than 4,400 with serious injuries, according to the Nigerien Agency for Road Safety. Speeding, drink-driving and the poor state of both the roads and cars remain the main causes of incidents. AFP The post 17 soldiers, others killed as buses collide in Niger appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: NAKAMBE/LUTTE ANTI-VECTORIELLE : Le gouverneur Yiyé Abraham Somdo appelle à une mobilisation permanente contre les gîtes larvaires
items.description: NAKAMBE/LUTTE ANTI-VECTORIELLE : Le gouverneur Yiyé Abraham Somdo appelle à une mobilisation permanente contre les gîtes larvaires Tenkodogo, 08 août 2026 (AIB) – Le gouverneur de la région du Nakambé, Yiyé Abraham Somdo, a lancé samedi la première édition des Journées nationales de lutte anti-vectorielle (JNLAV) à Tenkodogo. Il a invité les populations à faire de l'hygiène et de l'assainissement des réflexes quotidiens pour lutter contre le paludisme et les autres maladies à transmission vectorielle. La cérémonie de lancement s'est déroulée à partir de 7h30 en face du jardin du maire de Tenkodogo. Elle a été marquée par le curage d'un caniveau et l'élimination d'objets susceptibles de retenir l'eau et de favoriser la prolifération des moustiques. « Il ne s'agit pas d'une activité d'une seule journée ou de deux jours », a déclaré le gouverneur Yiyé Abraham Somdo, soulignant que les actions seront multipliées mensuellement. Le gouverneur a annoncé la mise en place d'une cellule composée de points focaux sectoriels et de représentants des différentes composantes de la population, notamment des jeunes et des femmes. Cette structure est chargée d'assurer la mobilisation régulière des populations autour des questions d'hygiène et d'assainissement. Au cours de la sortie terrain, les autorités ont constaté la présence de déchets et de points de rétention d'eau aux abords de certaines concessions. Les riverains ont été sensibilisés sur la nécessité de maintenir leur environnement propre et de détruire les gîtes larvaires. Le gouverneur a également insisté sur la responsabilité des collectivités territoriales, notamment dans le traitement des eaux stagnantes dans les rues et l'amélioration de la gestion des ordures ménagères. Selon le médecin épidémiologiste Saïdou Madi Bagaya, chef du service de lutte contre la maladie, la lutte anti-vectorielle nécessite une approche multisectorielle et ne saurait relever de la seule responsabilité des services de santé. Les actions prévues portent, entre autres, sur le curage des caniveaux, l'élimination des pneus usagés et des récipients abandonnés pouvant retenir les eaux de pluie, ainsi que la sensibilisation des ménages aux bonnes pratiques. M. Bagaya a précisé que quatre éditions sont prévues d'août à novembre 2026, en vue de renforcer progressivement la lutte contre les vecteurs. Pour le président de la délégation spéciale de la commune de Tenkodogo, Sami Bérenger Poda, cette initiative constitue une opportunité de mobiliser durablement les populations autour de gestes simples au sein des concessions. En lançant cette campagne, le gouverneur a invité les populations à transformer les opérations ponctuelles d'assainissement en habitudes quotidiennes pour contribuer collectivement à la prévention des maladies transmises par les moustiques. Agence d'Information du Burkina SM/ata

items.title: Carrick says being ‘careful’ with Mount as Man Utd draw with PSG
items.description: Michael Carrick said he had to be “careful” with Mason Mount after the England midfielder was involved in an injury scare during Manchester United’s 1-1 friendly draw with Paris Saint-Germain in Gothenburg on Saturday. Mount, who joined United from Chelsea in 2023, has been hampered by injury problems since arriving at Old Trafford and he lasted less than 20 minutes after starting against PSG. The 27-year-old appeared to suffer a foot injury in Sweden and, following discussions with coaches on the touchline, left the field to be replaced by Tyler Fletcher. “He (Mount) got kicked,” United manager Carrick told reporters. “We just wanted to be careful and look after him. “We’ve been lucky with injuries so far, so we wanted to be careful.” Post-match video footage showed Mount walking on to the United bus without any form of visible knee support or a protective boot. United, who will be competing in the 2026/27 Champions League alongside title-holders PSG next term after finishing third in the Premier League, were 1-0 down at the time of Mount’s injury. They had fallen behind in the second minute through an Ibrahim Mbaye goal even though French giants PSG were missing many of their star players. But Bryan Mbeumo equalised for United in the 32nd minute, with Amad Diallo playing him in after winning the ball back. There were more injury concerns for United early in the second half when their 40-year-old goalkeeper Tom Heaton suffered a right hamstring problem while rushing out to make a clearance. Mbeumo might have doubled his tally but for the fine form of PSG’s Matvey Safonov. The goalkeeper, however, left the pitch to jeers after escaping punishment for clattering into Joshua Zirkzee way outside of his area — an incident that may well have seen him sanctioned in a competitive match. At the other end, there were late chances for Fletcher, Shea Lacey and captain Bruno Fernandes, who linked up well with new arrival Youri Tielemans in an encouraging sign for Carrick. “I enjoyed it,” Carrick told MUTV, United’s in-house television station. “Good challenge. Slightly different with the way they play. We should’ve scored more goals.” The former United and England midfielder added: “It’s good for the boys sometimes to have to problem solve and find their own way and I thought we did that. That prepares them for the season as well. In that respect there were a lot of things that maybe people don’t always see that we were quite happy with. There were some good signs there.” United have two more friendly fixtures, against bitter rivals Leeds in Dublin on August 12 and AC Milan in the Polish city of Wroclaw three days later, before launching their Premier League campaign away to newly-promoted Hull on August 22. AFP The post Carrick says being ‘careful’ with Mount as Man Utd draw with PSG appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Sir Sam Jonah takes Abuja land dispute with Nigeria to ICC arbitration
items.description: Ghanaian businessman and mining executive Sir Sam Jonah has commenced international arbitration proceedings against the Nigerian government over a 501-hectare property in Abuja, escalating a long-running dispute over one of his major investments outside Ghana. The case, being heard under the auspices of the International Chamber of Commerce (ICC) in Paris, concerns the termination of a development lease covering the property near the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport. The investment is held through JonahCapital Nigeria Limited, a subsidiary of Sir Sam Jonah’s investment group. The financial value of the claim has not been publicly disclosed, although estimates have put the value of the property at about US$500 million based on prevailing property values in Abuja. River Park Estate at centre of dispute At the heart of the dispute is Plot 4 in Cadastral Zone E30, Lugbe West, a 501-hectare parcel allocated to JonahCapital in 2007 under Nigeria’s Mass Housing Scheme. The company subsequently developed the property into River Park Estate, a major residential and mixed-use development featuring homes, commercial facilities, healthcare centres, offices and places of worship. JonahCapital maintains that its development lease was due to remain in force until June 2030. The Federal Capital Development Authority (FCDA), however, terminated the lease in November 2025. JonahCapital has challenged the decision, describing the termination as unlawful and contrary to the terms of the development agreement. Infrastructure costs In its case, JonahCapital contends that Nigerian authorities failed to meet several obligations under the agreement. The company says the FCDA did not provide key infrastructure, including roads, electricity and water, leaving the developer to finance and construct the facilities at significant cost. It has also raised concerns about building approval fees and alleged that sections of the disputed property have been fenced off while the arbitration process is underway. JonahCapital further claims that the development has faced ownership claims from third parties, resulting in years of legal and administrative challenges. The allegations are yet to be determined by the arbitration tribunal. Wike: ‘Let arbitration take its course’ Nigeria’s Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, has confirmed that the matter has been taken to arbitration and said the government would respect the process. “The other party has gone to arbitration, and we say, ‘Okay, until you finish from arbitration,'” he said. Mr Wike has maintained that the government acted lawfully in recovering the property after the expiry of the lease. He has also disputed aspects of the development, arguing that some of the projects in question were undertaken by Paulo Homes Limited, a separate company engaged by JonahCapital to facilitate certain approvals. Criminal proceedings The commercial dispute is running alongside a separate criminal case involving Sir Sam Jonah and several other individuals before the Federal Capital Territory High Court. The 26-count case includes allegations of forgery of company documents and the unlawful allocation of shares in companies associated with the Abuja development. Sir Sam Jonah has denied the allegations. The charges are yet to be determined by the court. Ghana intervenes The dispute has also drawn the attention of the Ghanaian government amid concerns about the protection of Ghanaian investments in Nigeria. In late 2025, Sir Sam Jonah petitioned Ghana’s Minister for Foreign Affairs, Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, over what he described as actions by Nigerian regulatory authorities that threatened his interests in the investment. Mr Ablakwa subsequently raised concerns about the treatment of Ghanaian businesses operating in Nigeria at an ECOWAS Council of Ministers meeting in Abuja, citing the JonahCapital dispute. The Foreign Affairs Minister had earlier visited River Park Estate and expressed support for efforts to safeguard Ghanaian investments abroad. Why the ICC case matters By taking the dispute to ICC arbitration, JonahCapital has opted for an international dispute-resolution mechanism rather than relying solely on Nigeria’s domestic courts. International commercial arbitration is widely used in cross-border investment disputes and can provide a mechanism for parties to resolve contractual disagreements before an independent tribunal. The arbitration hearing date has not yet been announced, while the related criminal proceedings in Nigeria remain pending. Sir Sam Jonah is among Ghana’s most prominent business figures. He rose to prominence through the transformation of Ashanti Goldfields Company into one of Africa’s leading mining companies and later became President of AngloGold Ashanti following the 2004 merger between Ashanti Goldfields and AngloGold. He subsequently expanded his business interests into sectors including mining, energy and real estate across Africa. The Abuja development remains one of his major property investments outside Ghana.

items.title: 15 blocs opératoires rendus fonctionnels en 2 ans
items.description: Pour réduire les délais de prise en charge des femmes enceintes confrontées à des complications, le Sénégal accélère l’ouverture des blocs opératoires dans les centres de santé. Quinze d’entre eux ont déjà été rendus fonctionnels ces deux dernières années. Les autorités sanitaires ambitionnent d’en rendre fonctionnels 32 à travers le pays d’ici à 2027. La disponibilité des soins obstétricaux d’urgence constitue un axe majeur dans la lutte contre la mortalité maternelle et néonatale. Lors de la deuxième session du Comité de pilotage et de coordination des interventions en Santé reproductive, maternelle, néonatale, infantile, de l’adolescent et la nutrition (Srmnia-N), tenue vendredi 7 août, à Dakar, le directeur de la Santé de la mère et de l’enfant, le Dr Amadou Doucouré, a rappelé la nécessité de rapprocher les soins chirurgicaux des populations. « Durant ces dernières années, nous avons pu ouvrir 15 blocs opératoires dans des centres de santé. Soit ce sont des blocs qui étaient ouverts avant d’être fermés, soit ils étaient construits, mais n’avaient jamais été fonctionnels », a-t-il expliqué. Le ministère de la Santé et de l’Hygiène publique prévoit l’ouverture de nouveaux blocs dans plusieurs zones, notamment à Darou Mousty, Médina Gounass, Ranérou, Kanel et Podor. L’objectif est de rendre opérationnels 12 nouveaux blocs d’ici décembre 2026 et 3 autres d'ici fin 2027, pour atteindre le seuil cible de 32 structures fonctionnelles. Cette stratégie vise à limiter les longues évacuations vers les hôpitaux de référence et à réduire la pression sur les structures hospitalières. « L'ouverture de ces blocs au niveau des centres de santé permettra de diminuer la pression sur les hôpitaux régionaux et nationaux », a indiqué le Dr Doucouré. Malgré ces avancées, les hémorragies du post-partum restent le principal défi. Elles représentent près de 40 % des décès maternels au Sénégal. Pour y répondre, les autorités misent sur le renforcement des banques de sang, l’extension des centres régionaux de transfusion sanguine et l’utilisation de nouveaux équipements. Les indicateurs montrent toutefois une évolution positive. Selon l’Enquête démographique et de santé continue (Edsc 2023), le ratio de mortalité maternelle a continuellement chuté, passant de 392 décès/100 000 naissances vivantes en 2012 à 153 décès/100 000 naissances vivantes. Le processus d’ouverture des blocs opératoires dans les centres de santé existe depuis plusieurs années. Il a débuté en 1998, avec la maternité de Goudiry, avant de s’étendre progressivement. Mais, plusieurs défis demeurent, notamment la fonctionnalité permanente des infrastructures, la disponibilité des ressources humaines qualifiées et l’équipement des structures sanitaires. Le secrétaire général du ministère de la Santé et de l’Hygiène publique, Leroux Dramé, a appelé à une meilleure coordination des interventions en Srmnia-N. Il a souligné la nécessité de consolider les acquis et de renforcer l’engagement collectif des acteurs pour améliorer durablement les résultats sanitaires. M. Dramé a appelé à une meilleure articulation entre les structures publiques, les collectivités territoriales et les partenaires techniques et financiers afin d’optimiser les ressources et d’améliorer l’impact des programmes sur les populations. Amadou KÉBÉ

items.title: UGTT | Décès de Chamseddine Khelifi, SG de la Fédération générale du transport
items.description: C'est avec une immense tristesse, que l'Union générale tunisienne du travail (UGTT) a annoncé, samedi 8 août 2026, le décès de Chamseddine Khelifi, secrétaire général de la Fédération générale du transport. L'UGTT rappelle que Chamseddine Khelifi est une figure clé des luttes sociales menées ces dernières années dans le secteur et qu'il avait activement participé à l'organisation et à l'encadrement de nombreux mouvements syndicaux. Dans son communiqué, l'UGTT a également salué le parcours de Chamseddine Khelifi, un militant reconnu pour sa présence, son engagement et son intégrité et qui aura profondément empreint de son engagement le secteur du transport au cours des dernières années. « Sa disparition laisse un vide au sein de ses camarades et des travailleurs du secteur, qui retiennent de lui l'image d'un homme de conviction dévoué à la cause ouvrière et au dialogue social », ajoute la centrale syndicale. Et de préciser que Chamseddine Khelifi sera accompagné à sa dernière demeure demain dimanche 9 août 2026, après la prière de l'Asr cimetière de Gammarth ​(Le cortège funèbre partira de la Cité Riadh Bouselsela). items.title: Histoire de la nuit africaine: à Soweto, le Club Pelican, lieu de rencontres durant l'apartheid[4/10]
items.description: Son nom n’est désormais connu que des plus anciens, mais à Soweto, le Club Pelican était, dans les années 1970, un endroit incontournable pour ceux qui aimaient la musique et la fête. En plein apartheid, ce night-club, l’un des premiers du genre dans le township, offrait un espace afin de décompresser, faisant fi des lois de ségrégation, et permettait à des populations quotidiennement séparées de se croiser, le temps d’une soirée.

items.title: Kano spends N1.5bn on mass wedding
items.description: Gov. Abba Kabir-Yusuf of Kano State says the state government has expended N1.5 billion on mass wedding programme, covering medical screening, dowry, furniture, and other items for the couples. Gov. Yusuf made the disclosure on Saturday during a reception and the distribution of furniture, among other items, to the couples at the Kano State Government House. He said the present administration had committed over N1.5 billion to ensure the successful implementation of the programme and to provide comprehensive support to the newly married couples. “This expenditure covered medical screening for all the brides and grooms to safeguard their health and that of their future children. “Similarly, we provided the payment of N100,000 as dowry, in addition to another N100,000 as capital grant to serve as seed capital for starting a business and promoting self-reliance. “We also provided household furniture and essential items, including beds, mattresses, and other necessities to enable the couples to begin their married lives comfortably. “Government has also provided food items and other essential commodities to cushion the hardship they may encounter during the early days of their marriage,” he said. The governor called on the new couples to strive to maintain peace, harmony, mutual respect, and understanding in their homes. He reminded the couples that marriage “is an act of worship”, while urging them to conduct their matrimonial lives in accordance with the teachings of the Holy Qur’an and the Sunnah of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (SAW). Kabir-Yusuf said the mass wedding programme, known as Auren Gata, was one of the key campaign promises he made ahead of the 2023 general election. “Let me remind us that the Auren Gata programme was one of the key promises that we made during our campaign across all the 44 local government areas of Kano state ahead of the 2023 general elections. “Today, we have continued to fulfil that promise. Before this wedding ceremony, all prospective couples underwent a comprehensive screening process. “This included medical examinations to ascertain their health status, marriage counselling by qualified professionals, and participation in workshops and seminars designed by the Kano State Hisbah Board to prepare them for the responsibilities of married life,” he revealed. The governor seized the opportunity to congratulate the new couples as they begin a new chapter in their lives together. “As you were repeatedly advised during the counselling sessions, I urge you to be patient with one another, to uphold justice and fairness in your homes, to respect one another, and to live together in peace, harmony, and mutual understanding,” he prayed. The Chairman of the Northwest Governors’ Forum and Governor of Katsina State, Umar Dikko-Radda, commended Gov. Yusuf for the initiative, describing it as a programme aimed at improving the welfare and living conditions of the people of the state. Earlier, a prominent Islamic Cleric, Sheikh Abdullahi Bala-Lau, represented by Sheikh Kabir Gombe, said the initiative was capable of addressing insecurity and incessant protests spearheaded by idle youths. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that dignitaries present at the event included Gov. Umar Namadi of Jigawa and former governor of Kano State, Sen. Ibrahim Shekarau, among others. items.title: Mercato : Man City proche de boucler l'arrivée d'Ayoub Bouaddi pour 100 M€
items.description: L'international marocain Ayoub Bouaddi est plus que jamais proche de rejoindre Manchester City lors de ce mercato estival. Selon les informations dévoilées par le média français Foot Mercato, les négociations entre le club mancunien et le LOSC sont entrées dans leur phase finale, avec un optimisme grandissant du côté des dirigeants anglais pour sceller l'opération dans les prochains jours. Considéré comme l'une des priorités absolues de Manchester City pour renforcer son entrejeu, le jeune milieu de terrain de 18 ans pourrait faire l'objet d'un transfert record estimé à environ 100 millions d'euros. Un montant XXL qui placerait le pépite marocaine parmi les joueurs les plus chers de l'histoire du football national et africain lors d'un passage vers un grand d'Europe. Courtisé par plusieurs cadors européens après ses prestations remarquées sous les couleurs du LOSC, Bouaddi a vu les Citizens prendre une longueur d'avance décisive sur la concurrence. Le champion d'Angleterre en titre anticipe ainsi les grandes manœuvres au milieu de terrain, notamment en prévision des incertitudes entourant l'avenir de l'Espagnol Rodri, et voit en l'international marocain un profil d'avenir idéal pour porter son projet sportif. Les derniers détails administratifs et financiers entre Lille et Manchester City devraient être réglés incessamment avant l'officialisation de son arrivée en Premier League. items.title: Décès de Jorge Messi: Le Real Madrid et Barça présentent leurs condoléances à Lionel Messi
items.description: Après l'annonce du décès de la mort du père de Lionel Messi, ce samedi 8 août 2026, des clubs de football comme le Barça et le Real Madrid ont présenté leurs condoléances au multiple Ballon d'Or. «Le Real Madrid, son président et son conseil d'administration regrettent profondément la mort de Jorge Messi, le père de Leo Messi», lit-on dans un message de la «Maison Blanche». Le Real présente ses condoléances à Leo, à sa famille et à tous ses proches, tout en souhaitant que l'âme du défunt puisse reposer en paix. Le Barça, où Léo évoluait, rend hommage au père de l’emblématique footballeur Léo Messi. «Le président et le conseil d’administration du FC Barcelone expriment leurs plus sincères condoléances à la suite du décès de Jorge Messi, père du joueur et légende du Barça Lionel Messi, et adressent, au nom de toute la communauté blaugrana, leurs condoléances à la famille Messi», dit le club dans un message. Le Barça a tenu de remercier Jorge Messi pour son engagement envers le club, «pour lui avoir fait confiance lors des débuts de son fils Leo ainsi que durant les années les plus glorieuses de sa carrière de footballeur». items.title: Ghanaian paediatric oncologist Dr. Emmanuella Amoako wins 2026 Roux Prize
items.description: Ghanaian paediatric oncologist Dr. Emmanuella Amoako has been named the recipient of the 2026 Roux Prize, becoming the first Ghanaian to win the prestigious global award for outstanding contributions to population health. The award, announced by the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME) at the University of Washington, recognises individuals who demonstrate exceptional use of health evidence and data to improve the lives of populations. Dr. Amoako was honoured for her work in advancing childhood cancer care, particularly efforts aimed at promoting early diagnosis, improving access to treatment and strengthening survival outcomes for children diagnosed with cancer. Her work has focused significantly on strengthening paediatric oncology services at the Cape Coast Teaching Hospital, where she has championed measures to improve the early detection of childhood cancers, referral pathways and access to specialised care. IHME said her contribution illustrates the importance of translating health data and locally generated evidence into practical interventions, particularly in resource-constrained settings where access to specialised childhood cancer services remains a challenge. As part of the recognition, Dr. Amoako will receive a US$100,000 prize for her contribution to improving population health through evidence-based approaches. Her achievement adds to a growing list of recognitions for her work in healthcare delivery. She was recently named among Channel One TV’s Top 10 Community Legends, an initiative that celebrates individuals whose work has made a significant difference in their communities. The Roux Prize was established in 2013 by philanthropists David and Barbara Roux to honour individuals who have demonstrated exceptional impact in population health through the innovative application of health evidence and data. Dr. Amoako’s recognition places the spotlight on the potential of evidence-driven healthcare interventions developed within Ghana to address major health challenges and improve outcomes for vulnerable groups, particularly children. Her work in paediatric oncology has also highlighted the importance of timely diagnosis and coordinated referral systems in improving the prospects of children with cancer, especially where specialist services are limited. The 2026 award therefore represents not only a personal milestone for Dr. Amoako but also a significant recognition of Ghanaian expertise in using evidence to strengthen healthcare delivery.

items.title: Kingsley Atta secures Bantama NPP Chairmanship with slim 4-vote victory in re-run
items.description: Delegates of the New Patriotic Party in the Bantama Constituency have elected Kingsley Atta as the new Constituency Chairman in a keenly contested re-run election held on Saturday, August 8, 2026, at the Kumasi Cultural Centre. Mr. Atta secured victory with a slim margin of 4 votes, defeating his closest contender, Fiifi Mensah, in an election supervised by officials of the Electoral Commission and observed by national and regional executives of the NPP. In certified results declared by the EC’s Returning Officer, Kingsley Atta polled 570 votes representing 50.2%, whilst the incumbent Chairman, Fiifi Mensah, obtained 566 votes, representing 49.8%. The tight margin marks a sharp contrast to the annulled election held on Sunday, July 12, 2026, where Mr. Atta had won by a landslide. The re-run followed the NPP’s National Steering Committee’s decision to annul the initial constituency executive election, citing breaches of party directives and electoral regulations. In that election, Kingsley Atta defeated the incumbent Chairman, Fiifi Mensah, with 714 votes, representing 72.8% of the 995 valid votes cast. Fiifi Mensah obtained 267 votes, representing 27.2%. Addressing delegates after his victory, the newly elected Chairman, Kingsley Atta, expressed gratitude to delegates for the confidence reposed in him despite the significant reduction in the number of votes he received compared to the initial election. “Today, the delegates have spoken. I am humbled by this mandate. The numbers may be different, but the task ahead is the same,” he said. He pledged to prioritise unity within the party and work to deliver victory for the NPP in the Bantama Constituency in the 2028 general elections. “We cannot afford to go into 2028 divided. I will be Chairman for all, and my door is open to everyone, including my brother Fiifi. To my supporters, let us celebrate with decorum. This victory belongs to the party,” Mr. Atta added. In a show of sportsmanship, the outgoing Chairman, Fiifi Mensah, walked straight to the seat of the newly-elected Chairman, Kingsley Atta, and hugged him in a warm handshake. He congratulated Mr. Atta and all the newly elected executive members on their victory. Mr. Atta described the gesture as a sign of maturity and unity. In an interview with the media, Fiifi Mensah pledged to sustain his efforts to help the party secure victory in the next general elections, despite his defeat. “I accept the verdict of the delegates in good faith. The decision has been made, and I respect it. I will remain committed to the party and will do all I can to ensure victory for the party in 2028,” he added. Reacting to the annulled election, he said the re-run result had vindicated his claim that the first election was not conducted fairly. “The outcome of today’s re-run has only confirmed what we raised from the beginning. That election was conducted on unfair grounds and did not reflect the true will of the delegates. In that election I lost by 447 votes, but in today’s election I lost by only 4 votes,” he stated. Delegates also elected Vincent Kofi Amoabeng as First Vice Chairman, Frank Boateng as Second Vice Chairman, Douglas Acheampong (Unopposed) as Constituency Secretary, Kwadwo Adu as Assistant Secretary, and Eric Mensah as Constituency Organiser. The remaining elected officers include Nana Boakye as Youth Organiser, Vivian Arthur as Treasurer, Josephine Ama Poma as Women’s Organiser, Kingsford Addai as Communications Director, and Afram Tuffour as Nasara Coordinator. Representatives of the Ashanti Regional and National Executives, as well as the Member of Parliament for Bantama, Francis Asenso-Boakye, were present to observe the process. They expressed satisfaction with how the re-run was conducted. Speaking after the results were declared, the Bantama MP, Francis Asenso-Boakye, congratulated the winner and urged all members to unite behind the new executives. “The time for division is over. The focus now is on unity. Whoever won or lost, we must all rally behind one goal to work together to make Dr. Mahamudu Bawumia the next president in the 2028 general elections in order to continue the good works and legacy of President Akufo-Addo,” the MP stated. He commended delegates for conducting themselves peacefully and thanked the Electoral Commission and security agencies for ensuring a transparent process. The new executives are expected to take office in the coming days to immediately begin reorganizing the constituency and mobilising support for the NPP’s flagbearer, Dr. Mahamudu Bawumia, ahead of the 2028 elections.

items.title: Port du casque obligatoire : Vers un duel à la « Tom and Jerry » entre la police et les récalcitrants
items.description: Face à un bilan sanglant de près de 650 morts sur place en seulement sept mois, le gouvernement burkinabè durcit radicalement sa position sur la sécurité routière. Ce samedi 8 août 2026, le ministre de la Sécurité, Mahamadou Sana, a lancé un ultime avertissement aux usagers de la route, dénonçant la persistance des comportements à risque malgré deux années de sensibilisation. Entre l'annonce de consignes de refoulement systématique pour les motocyclistes sans protection et une critique acerbe des excuses « esthétiques », le message est clair : la vie humaine prime désormais sur toute autre considération. Le ton est monté d'un cran au ministère de la Sécurité. Dans une vidéo publiée ce samedi, le ministre Mahamadou Sana s’est adressé avec une franchise désarmante aux 10 % d’usagers de la route qui continuent de faire « la sourde oreille » face au port obligatoire du casque. Les chiffres avancés par le ministre font froid dans le dos : de janvier à juillet 2026, 649 personnes ont perdu la vie directement sur le lieu d'un accident de la route. Un décompte qui ne prend même pas en compte les décès survenus ultérieurement dans les centres hospitaliers. Face à cette tragédie, Mahamadou Sana a usé d'une métaphore frappante pour rappeler la fragilité humaine : « Personne n’a une tête en fer ici. Ou bien, en touchant le goudron, vous avez l’impression d’avoir affaire à un matelas ? ». Le ministre a vigoureusement balayé les prétextes souvent invoqués pour éviter le casque. Il a notamment fustigé l'attitude de certains internautes qualifiant les images de sensibilisation de « montages générés par l’Intelligence artificielle ». Plus surprenant encore, il a interpellé les femmes refusant le casque à cause de leurs mèches de cheveux. « Si vous mettez des mèches qui vous empêchent de mettre le casque, un jour vous ne serez plus là, mais la mèche sera là », a-t-il martelé, rappelant que l'esprit de « révolution » ne saurait s'accommoder de telles futilités. L'époque de la simple pédagogie semble révolue. Si la vidéo-verbalisation et le déploiement de l'ONASER sont déjà effectifs, de nouvelles instructions ont été données à la police et à la gendarmerie. Désormais, tout motocycliste sans casque sera refoulé et contraint de rebrousser chemin. Le ministre a même prévenu que si l’incivisme persistait, les forces de l'ordre et les contrevenants finiraient par se « pourchasser comme Tom and Jerry ». À l’approche de la rentrée scolaire de septembre, l’accent est également mis sur la protection des enfants. Le ministre a déploré l'attitude de certains parents qui portent un casque mais oublient d'en équiper leur progéniture installée à l'arrière. Prenant l'exemple de Lomé, où la discipline est de rigueur pour le conducteur comme pour le passager, il aspire à voir une transformation similaire des mentalités au Burkina Faso. Enfin, les cyclistes, accusés de brûler régulièrement les feux tricolores, sont prévenus : leur « temps arrive » également dans cette vaste opération d'assainissement de la circulation routière.
